theorems.title: Theorem (a complex orthogonal to all positive-current cells)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (a complex orthogonal to all positive-current cells).** Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic zero and \(\mathcal S\) the category of smooth \(t\mathfrak{sl}_2(k)[t]\)-modules with algebraic integer energy grading and degree-preserving maps. In the unbounded category \(D(\mathcal S)\), the localizing subcategory generated by the trivial modules \(k\langle u\rangle\), \(u\in\mathbb Z\), is strictly contained in the subcategory of complexes with jointly augmentation-torsion cohomology. There is a complex \(X_{\mathrm{lin}}\) with nonzero jointly torsion \(H^{-n}(X_{\mathrm{lin}})\) for every \(n\ge1\), zero cohomology in nonnegative degrees, and
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal S)}(k\langle u\rangle,X_{\mathrm{lin}}[j])=0
 \qquad(u,j\in\mathbb Z).
\]

theorems.title: Theorem (a critical affine complex orthogonal to the regular top)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (a critical affine complex orthogonal to the regular top).** Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional, complex and simple, with long roots of squared length \(2\). Put \(U_+=U(t\mathfrak g[t])\), and let \(W=A_\ell\otimes_{U_+}\mathbb C\) be the affine module with regular horizontal top. At raw level \(\ell=-h^\vee\), in the ordinary unbounded derived category of algebraically energy-graded smooth affine modules, \(\mathscr C=\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle u\rangle:u\in\mathbb Z\}\) is strictly contained in \(D_{\mathfrak a}\). There is a nonzero \(Z\in D_{\mathfrak a}\) with \(\operatorname{RHom}(W\langle u\rangle,Z)=0\) for every \(u\). Both its cellular counit and its intrinsic torsion counit have zero source.

theorems.title: Example (the dual numbers)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (the dual numbers).** Take \(A=k[x]/(x^2)\). The ordinary centre is all of \(A\). A derivation is determined by \(f(x)=a+bx\), and
\[
0=f(x^2)=2x f(x)=2ax
\]
forces \(a=0\). Since \(A\) is commutative, inner derivations vanish. Hence
\[
HH^0(A)=k\oplus kx,\qquad HH^1(A)=k\delta,
\qquad \delta(x)=x.
\]
The class \(x\) in degree zero acts on an \(A\)-module by multiplication. The degree-one cochain \(\delta\) takes an algebra element as input. It gives \(\delta(1)=0\) and \(\delta(x)=x\), so the Gerstenhaber bracket with the degree-zero class is \([\delta,x]=x\). Its value on the unit alone would miss this bracket.

theorems.title: Recognition theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Recognition theorem.** Suppose \(V\) is any unbounded dg chiral algebra over a characteristic-zero field on \(\mathbb A^1\), with a genuine closed horizontal unit. For every coherent coassociative pointing \(u:J\to C_V\), the maps \(\Theta\) and \(\Psi\) are inverse equivalences between \(\mathcal X(C_V,u)\) and \(\mathcal A_C(C_V,u)\). No homotopy from \(u\) to the genuine unit pointing is required. The equivalence is natural under all pointed coalgebra maps between these objects, including those that preserve no chosen presentation. [Arbitrary-pointing recognition](#ref-ch07-02).

theorems.title: Unitization theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Unitization theorem.** Let \(W\) be an arbitrary unbounded, possibly noncommutative and nonconstant nonunital dg chiral algebra on \(\mathbb A^1_k\). Suppose its coherent pointing \(u\) admits a strict closed horizontal degree-zero state \(a:\omega_X\to W\) such that
\[
H^0(a)=H^0(u_1):\omega_X\longrightarrow H^0(W).
\]
Then restriction along \(i\) induces equivalences on both complete character and action fibres. Consequently \(\Theta\) and \(\Psi\) are inverse for \((C_W,u)\), naturally on the full stated subcategory. The displayed equality is only in ordinary cohomology. Equality of \(a\) and \(u_1\) in full derived Hom is not a hypothesis. [Unitization from an ordinary horizontal representative](#ref-ch07-04).

theorems.title: Binary exterior-source theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Binary exterior-source theorem.** The specified comparison
\[
\rho_B:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A,B)\longrightarrow N(B)
\]
is an equivalence for every ordinary algebraic dg vertex algebra \(B\), with arbitrary translation, no commutativity assumption and no boundedness assumption. [Logarithmic quotient construction](#ref-ch07-07).

theorems.title: Theorem (finite exterior sources)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (finite exterior sources).** Let \(A_r=\Lambda(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r)\) with \(r\geq1\) finite, all generators of degree one, and differential and translation zero. In the ordinary algebraic localization above, \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A_r,X)\) is represented by the following tuples in \(X\otimes\Omega_\bullet\), for every ordinary dg vertex target \(X\). Choose the order \(1,\ldots,r\). For each nonempty subset \(I\) take two entries \(a_I,s_I\) of degrees \(2-|I|,1-|I|\), respectively, and put \(L_I=(s_I)_{(0)}\). Sum over decompositions \(I=P\sqcup Q\) into nonempty blocks with \(\max I\in Q\). Let \(\varepsilon(P,Q)\) be the sign of listing \(P\), then \(Q\), in their increasing orders. The equations are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 d a_I&=\sum_{P,Q}\varepsilon(P,Q)L_Pa_Q,\\
 d s_I&=T a_I-\sum_{P,Q}\varepsilon(P,Q)(-1)^{1-|P|}L_Ps_Q .
\end{aligned}
\]
Singletons have empty sums. For \(I=\{1,2\}\) the only split allowed is \(\{1\}|\{2\}\), so the two equations give the terms \(u_{1(0)}e_2\) and \(T\beta-u_{1(0)}u_2\) of the binary calculation. For \(r=3\) they give exactly the fourteen entries above, including \(c,s\). For \(X=\mathbb C\) only the \(r\) singleton companions and \(\binom r2\) pair tops can be constants of degree zero. The singleton tops give closed one-forms on the simplex. This computes
\[
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A_r,\mathbb C)
\simeq \mathbb C_{\mathrm{disc}}^{\,r+\binom r2}\times K(\mathbb C^r,1).
\]

theorems.title: The automorphism test for a genuine Heisenberg action
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Which automorphisms could escape the scalar-loop measurement? Form the square-zero extension
\[
X_1=H\oplus\epsilon_1H,
\qquad |\epsilon_1|=1,
\quad \epsilon_1^2=d\epsilon_1=T\epsilon_1=0,
\]
with its canonical section and projection. Work in the genuine pointed slice \(\mathcal V_{H//H}\), which retains both the under-\(H\) and over-\(H\) homotopies. Let \(U\) be the space of its automorphisms of \(X_1\) that induce the identity on state cohomology. At the trivial action \(\alpha_0\), define
\[
\Phi=\operatorname{hofib}_0
\bigl[F_{\alpha_0}\xrightarrow{\delta}K(\mathbb C,1)\bigr],
\]
where \(F_{\alpha_0}\) is the connected component of \(\alpha_0\). The scalar section makes \(\Phi\) connected, and the genuine loop comparison gives
\[
U\simeq\Omega\Phi,
\qquad
q_B\text{ is an equivalence}
\Longleftrightarrow
F^0\text{ is connected and }U\text{ is contractible}.
\]
The first condition tests whether a whole component escapes the two labels. The second tests for extra automorphisms within the trivial component. Loop concatenation adds scalars and has identity \(0\). Composition of endomorphisms multiplies their detected scalars and has identity \(1\). A splitting over the scalar set alone would give no splitting for composition.
theorems.source_paragraph: Which automorphisms could escape the scalar-loop measurement? Form the square-zero extension

theorems.title: Theorem (components of the genuine Heisenberg action space)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (components of the genuine Heisenberg action space).** Over \(\mathbb C\), for the single degree-one exterior generator and the rank-one boundary \(V_\kappa\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), the original roof comparison \(q_B\) is a weak equivalence. The charge and constant give all its components. Each component has additive fundamental group \(\mathbb C\) and vanishing higher homotopy groups. Thus \(F\simeq\mathbb C^2_{\mathrm{disc}}\times K(\mathbb C,1)\).

theorems.title: Theorem (finite-colour exterior actions)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (finite-colour exterior actions).** Let \(H=V_\kappa\) be the rank-one vacuum Heisenberg algebra over \(\mathbb C\), with \(J_{(1)}J=\kappa\mathbf1\) and \(\kappa\ne0\). Let \(V\) be finite dimensional in cohomological degree one and put \(A_V=\Lambda(V)\) with zero differential and translation. In \(\mathcal V\), the ordinary algebraic dg vertex category localized at quasi-isomorphisms of whole state complexes, let \(F(V)\) be the homotopy fibre over \(1_H\) of restriction along \(h\mapsto1\otimes h\) from \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(A_V\otimes H,H)\) to \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H,H)\). There is a weak equivalence, natural under all linear substitutions of the generators,
\[
 F(V)\simeq
 \bigl(V^*\oplus V^*\oplus(\Lambda^2V)^*\bigr)_{\mathrm{disc}}
 \times K(V^*,1).
\]
The first two functionals are the unary charge \(\lambda\) and constant \(\beta\). For a chosen basis of \(V\), the homotopy fibre over any specified tuple of genuine actions on the coordinate lines, with paths identifying the restrictions with those actions, is weakly equivalent to the discrete space \(\big((\Lambda^2V)^*\big)_{\mathrm{disc}}\).

theorems.title: Strict three-spectator theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Strict three-spectator theorem.** For \(r=3\), every \(b_j,N_{ij}\ge0\), every positive odd \(\mu\), and every charge \(q\ge2\),
\[
H^n(D_{3,q}(b,N;\mu))=0\qquad(n<q).
\]
This holds over the whole polynomial spectator base, including simultaneous collisions, and in every homogeneity. The conclusion \(H^n=0\) for \(q\ge2\) and \(n<q\), with positive odd \(\mu\), also holds for \(r=2\) and arbitrary nonnegative \(b,N\), and for arbitrary \(r\) when every \(b_j=0\) and \(N_{ij}\ge0\). [Three-spectator proof](#ref-ch07-08).

theorems.title: Theorem (four spectators at charge five)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (four spectators at charge five).** For \(b=(1,1,1,1)\), \(\mu=1\) and arbitrary \(N_{ij}\ge0\), one has \(H^n(D_{4,5})=0\) for \(n<5\). With one spectator selected, four marks remain and its marked de Rham cohomology vanishes in form degrees zero through two. With two selected, antisymmetry kills the only possible zero-form class below total degree five. With three or more selected the total degree is already at least six. In the unselected column the only possible class below five maps injectively under the first residue from form degree four to form degree three of the one-selected column. [The charge-five filtration](#ref-ch07-09).

theorems.title: Example (A current insertion after Laurent completion)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
What can a second field insertion do on the smaller space? Take \(F=\mathbb C\) and let the third states be one-quantum states of the neutral level-one current. Write \(\Omega\) for its vacuum, \(J(u)=\sum_n J_nu^{-n-1}\) for its field, and \(w_j=J_{-j-1}\Omega/(j+1)\) for \(j\ge0\). Insert the field at \(u\) and project onto the vacuum, with \(\langle\Omega,\Omega\rangle=1\). Only \(J_{j+1}\) can remove this quantum. Its commutator with \(J_{-j-1}\) is \(j+1\), so the amplitude is \(\langle\Omega,J(u)w_j\rangle=u^{-j-2}\). [The free-current contraction](03-local-fields.md#heisenberg-current).

Use the same formal parameter \(u=p\) for this insertion. On a finite sum of spectator states the amplitudes have a common bound on their pole orders. We may therefore multiply each by the corresponding Laurent series of pair states and add. On \(s_m\) this prescription gives
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{m} p^j v\,\langle\Omega,J(p)w_j\rangle
       =(m+1)p^{-2}v .
\]
The inputs converge coefficient by coefficient in the joint completion. The coefficient of \(p^{-2}\) in the outputs never stabilises. Keeping the insertion at an independent coordinate gives the explanation in the free field itself. The infinite sum there is \(v/[u(u-p)]\), expanded in \(p/u\). It has a pole at the very value \(u=p\) at which the second insertion was requested. A finite spectator span was enough to define that insertion on the algebraic tensor. Enlarging its domain requires control of the poles of the states being admitted.

theorems.title: Example (finite-rank matrices)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (finite-rank matrices).** Label the independent states in the example by rows and the powers of the separation by columns. The \(j\)th column has its only nonzero entry in row \(j\). Which matrices can a finite sum of products produce? In the space \(V=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N}\) of all complex sequences consider the map

\[
V\otimes_{\mathbb C}V\longrightarrow
\mathbb C^{\mathbb N\times\mathbb N},
\qquad f\otimes g\longmapsto(f_i g_j)_{i,j\geq0}.
\]
{#eq-sequence-tensor-map}

Its image consists of the matrices of finite rank. For \(\sum_{a=1}^r f^a\otimes g^a\), column \(j\) is \(\sum_a g^a_j f^a\). Conversely, choose a basis of the column space of a finite-rank matrix. The coefficients of the successive columns along each basis vector form the required second sequence. The diagonal matrix \((\delta_{ij})\) has infinitely many independent columns.

theorems.title: Lemma (finite coefficient span)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Lemma (finite coefficient span).** A vector-valued Laurent series with exponents bounded below comes from \(V\otimes_F F((q))\) exactly when its coefficients span a finite-dimensional subspace of \(V\).

theorems.title: Proposition (completed bar augmentation)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Proposition (completed bar augmentation).** The augmentation \(\mathcal B_z(T)\to S_z(T)\) multiplies the length-zero coefficient into \(T\), kills positive lengths, and is a quasi-isomorphism. [Rational evaluation on the completed incoming bar, Proposition 1](#ref-ch08-02).

theorems.title: Theorem — finite radial current comparison
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem — finite radial current comparison.** Assume the specified coherent smooth affine–right-\(Y\) realization, its tensor–Hom adjunction and full unit for ordinary unbounded \(Y\)-modules, its algebraic cofree model and common mode-cutoff actions. Assume also that every bounded-below smooth complex with jointly locally nilpotent positive-current cohomology belongs to the localizing category generated by \(W_K\), and that the derived ideal triangle expresses each \(Y_F\)-module by two complexes inflated from \(U_F\). Here inflation uses the augmentation \(Y_F\to U_F\), and the localizing category is closed under shifts, cones and arbitrary coproducts. Then, for every finite \(d\geq2\), every ordinary unbounded tuple \(M_1,\ldots,M_d\), and every \(X\in D_{\mathcal N}(A_K)\), the actual evaluation gives an equivalence

\[
\Xi_T(X):
R\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sm}(A_K)}
 \bigl(X,\mathcal W_K\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{Y_K}S_{\mathbf a}(T)\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I_d(X;T).
\]

The comparison retains the outgoing line action, all its specified higher compatibilities, and every additional commuting incoming right action. At the regular tuple it retains all \(d\) incoming regular right actions. Its coefficient evaluations are the rational maps \(\eta_{M_1,\ldots,M_d}\) and their original affine restrictions \(b_{M_1,\ldots,M_d}\). The theorem uses the bar and scalar-extension orders stated above. [The radial finite-puncture current recipient, equation (45)](#ref-ch08-03).

theorems.title: Counterexample (substitution on the radial field)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Counterexample (substitution on the radial field).** A separately completed nested tensor need not have that domain. In a three-point shape chart,

\[
f=\sum_{n\geq0}q^n\lambda^{-n^2}\in\mathbb C(\lambda)((q)).
\]

The substitution \(\lambda=zq\) would give

\[
\sum_{n\geq0}z^{-n^2}q^{n-n^2}.
\]

Its outer \(q\)-orders have no lower bound, so it is not in \(\mathbb C((z^{-1}))((q))\). The terms tend to zero before substitution and fail to do so afterwards. This is an obstruction to extending that substitution continuously to the entire radial field.

theorems.title: The full three-pole comparison for a finite-total spectator
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For a constant input \(T=T_{12}\otimes_{\mathbb C}M_3\), distinguish the joint intermediate object from the factorized one.
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_1&=S_w(T_{12})\otimes_{\mathbb C}M_3,\\
E&=S_w^{12}(T),\\
c&:E_1\hookrightarrow E.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both spaces carry the interaction of lines 1 and 2. In \(E\) the \(p\)-completion includes the third state. In \(E_1\) the third module is tensored on after that completion. The map \(c\) includes the resulting coefficient arrays. The pair \(T_{12}\) may be correlated and unbounded. If \(H^\bullet(M_3)\) has finite **total** dimension, \(c\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Assume in addition the coherent smooth realization and the full tensor–Hom unit used in the finite radial comparison. Then the three-pole evaluation reaches the endpoint obtained by completing the pair independently. It preserves the affine restriction and the unit of that adjunction on the outgoing module. The comparison diagram commutes strictly on the displayed algebraic bars and with the specified coherent homotopies after smooth replacement. A fixed left comb admits stagewise comparisons when each newly attached spectator has finite-total cohomology. Finite dimension in each degree does not suffice. [Finite-total native comparison](#atlas-c-horizontal-full-three-pole-native-finite-total).

theorems.title: Theorem (three-pole evaluation)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (three-pole evaluation).** The entire three-pole rational current resolution has an evaluation on a resolved model for \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)\). The theorem holds for arbitrary constant ordinary dg inputs, in particular the regular triple \(Y^{\otimes3}\). Let \(M=T_{12}\), \(N=M_3\), \(A=Y^{\otimes2}\) and \(B=Y\). Resolve the two inputs separately by the augmented bars
\[
R_M=\operatorname{Bar}_A(A,M),\qquad R_N=\operatorname{Bar}_B(B,N).
\]
Write \(F_3(V,W)\) for the underlying array intersection just defined, with \(V\) in the completed pair and \(W\) in the spectator position. With the pair-sum twist on its free heads, \(F_3(R_M,R_N)\) augments by a quasi-isomorphism to \(L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)\). For the evaluation target, replace the free right heads in the two bars by \(P^{\otimes2}\) and \(P\), respectively. Call the resulting bars \(T_M,T_N\). Their ordinary bar differentials give \(F_3(T_M,T_N)\) its differential.

Let \(P_c^D\) be the three-pole rational current resolution over \(D\). For \(\pi\in P_c^D\), expand \(\Delta^{(3)}(\pi)\) in the three affine heads. The direct expansion gives algebraic rational rows with common lower bounds. The factorization \(\Delta^{(3)}=(\Delta^{(12)}\otimes1)\Delta^{(12|3)}\) gives a second estimate. Each outer coefficient uses finitely many third heads, and applying the inner tensorator leaves them fixed. The two estimates put the same kernel in \(F_3(P^{\otimes2},P)\). The evaluation is the balanced chain map
\[
\begin{aligned}
\eta:P_c^D\otimes_{Y_D}F_3(R_M,R_N)&\longrightarrow F_3(T_M,T_N),\\
\pi\otimes(x\otimes y)&\longmapsto\Delta^{(3)}(\pi)\cdot(x\otimes y).
\end{aligned}
\]
The dot multiplies the heads and retains all letters and both terminal vectors, with the tensor signs. At each outer order a finite convolution of finite spectator spans suffices. The bound depends on the resolved word and the output order and permits arbitrarily long horizontal words in the incoming bars. In the chain identity the right twist of \(\Delta^{(3)}\) cancels the twist of the free heads. This explains the ordinary differential in the target.

theorems.title: Counterexample (an acyclic test over the common ring)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Counterexample (an acyclic test over the common ring).** A functor on derived tests must take an acyclic test to zero. The ordinary Hom formula over \(D\) can fail even on an exact sequence of three modules. Let \(g=p+s\). Substitution \(p=-s\) maps \(D\) to \(\mathbb C((s))\) and kills \(g\), so \(g\) is a nonunit. The complex
\[
E=(D\xrightarrow{g}D\longrightarrow D/g),
\qquad E^0=D,\quad E^1=D,\quad E^2=D/g,
\]
is acyclic, but \(H^0\operatorname{Hom}_D(E,D)=D/g\ne0\). Indeed multiplication by \(g\) is injective in the domain \(D\), and \(\operatorname{Hom}_D(D/g,D)=0\). Dualizing leaves the cokernel of multiplication by \(g\) in degree zero. Let \(W_D\) be the scalar extension to \(D\) of the regular-top affine object in the tensor–Hom realization. For trivial incoming coefficient, the ordinary current formula on the acyclic smooth test \(W_D\otimes_D E\) retracts onto this nonacyclic Hom complex. Thus that formula cannot define the proposed functor on arbitrary derived \(D\)-tests. The field and constant ground-field test theorems retain their stated scope. [The ordinary-Hom counterexample](#atlas-c-horizontal-common-ring-hom-counterexample).

theorems.title: Theorem (four-pole evaluation)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (four-pole evaluation).** Take constant ordinary pair inputs \(M,N\) over \(A=Y^{\otimes2}\), and write \(F_4(M,N)=L_*^{\mathrm{fac}}(M\otimes N)\). For each pair \(V=M,N\) take the bars \(R_V=\operatorname{Bar}_A(A,V)\) and \(T_V=\operatorname{Bar}_A(P^{\otimes2},V)\). Over \(D_*\), the four-pole resolution \(P_{c,*}^{(4)}\) has the evaluation
\[
P_{c,*}^{(4)}\otimes_{Y_{D_*}}F_4(R_M,R_N)\longrightarrow F_4(T_M,T_N),
\qquad \pi\otimes b\longmapsto\Delta^{(4)}(\pi)\cdot b .
\]
The source bars carry the four-point interaction and the target bars their ordinary bar differential. To see why the source resolves the stated intersection, contract an acyclic first input over \(\mathbb C\). Perturb its contraction first by the internal \(12\) kernel. A term of order \(e\) contributes \(q^e s_1^{-e}\) on the radial side and \(p_1^e\) in the first completed pair. It respects the conic bound and acts only in that pair. Next perturb by the four cross-pair kernels. All have positive outer order with finitely many factorwise operators in each coefficient. The resulting series converges on both sides and preserves finite tensor rank there. Interchanging the pairs proves invariance under a quasi-isomorphism in either input.

There are two estimates on one and the same resolution word. For \(\pi\) in the four-pole resolution extended from distinct positions to \(D_*\), the direct expansion of \(\Delta^{(4)}(\pi)\) satisfies the conic estimate. Its factorization
\[
\Delta^{(4)}=(\Delta^{(12)}\otimes\Delta^{(34)})\Delta^{(12|34)}
\]
has finitely many tensors of rational pair heads at each \(q\)-coefficient. Each inner tensorator acts only on its own head. Thus multiplying the independent free bar heads by this kernel lands in the same intersection with two affine heads in each target bar. The radial shuffle respects the multiplication. The comparison with the outer binary evaluation uses the two rational pair heads before applying their respective inner tensorators. Both sides carry the same right actions, affine restriction and unit normalization on the resolved words. The construction supplies a map on all the stated coefficients, including the regular inputs, without a finite-total cohomology hypothesis. [Four-pole rational tensorator](#atlas-c-horizontal-four-pole-rational-tensorator) · [Evaluations on the two factorized domains](#ref-ch08-06).

theorems.title: Example (the ray and its wall)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (the ray and its wall).** Apply \(D\) once more to \(b_1\). A test supported in the open upper chamber sees no derivative of the gate. A test at the common endpoint sees \(D[H(t)r_1]=C_1\) with exactly the orientation of the opening calculation. The endpoint form contributes \(DQ_1=-C_1\), so the sum is zero. The two tests account distributionally for \(D^2b_1=0\).

theorems.title: Theorem — finite marked Ward calculus
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem — finite marked Ward calculus.** With the stated compatible flats, internal gates, finite pole and jet orders, upward-proper coefficient support and canonical scalar extension, \(\mathcal D\mathcal M_I\subseteq\mathcal M_I\). For a scalar coefficient \(K\) with \(q\) marked factors, its derivative consists of four finite sums:

\[
DK=\mathcal B(K)+\mathcal S(K)+\mathcal V(K)+\mathcal C(K).
\]

Here \(\mathcal B\) replaces a ray by an additional mark with sign \((-1)^q\); \(\mathcal S\) takes the residues of entire complex-parallel scalar classes; \(\mathcal V\) takes the oriented real boundaries of whole simplified gates; and \(\mathcal C\) is the sum over closed critical marked flats. For each such flat the coefficients in \(\mathcal C(K)\) are annular moments of the whole weighted, gated normal kernel. The derivative of \(KF\) also includes \((-1)^qK\mathcal DF\). Old normal degrees contribute their Koszul sign, and every residue differentiates the entire remaining coefficient and field family to the required finite normal order.

theorems.title: Example (A contact with a third current present)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Insert another closed current \(\widehat J_3\). Put \(Q_{ij}=Q_1(n_{ij})\), \(C_{ij}=C_1(n_{ij})\), and \(E_{23}=E_2(z_2-z_3)\). The labels \(1,2,3\) are distinct and their positions can vary. There are three single contractions. Combining \(1,2\) first produces \(Q_{12}\) before the third field enters. Combining \(2,3\) first produces \(E_{23}\) before the first field enters. Both orders give the joint current
\[
 :\widehat p_1\widehat J_2\widehat J_3:
 +\hbar Q_{12}\widehat J_3+\hbar Q_{13}\widehat J_2
 +\hbar E_{23}\widehat p_1 .
\]
On a test supported where \(z_3\) stays away from both \(z_1\) and \(z_2\), the only contribution to its differential is \(-\hbar C_{12}\widehat J_3\). Indeed \(DQ_{13}=-C_{13}\) and \(DE_{23}=r_2(z_2-z_3)\) both vanish on that support, and the three remaining fields are closed. A test that meets the first two endpoints can read the contact with the third field still present. The mapping cone keeps this term available for gluing, together with its sign.

On another test, keep all three heights apart and bring \(z_2\) to \(z_3\). Both mixed contacts vanish there. The term \(\hbar r_2(u)\widehat p_1\) survives, with \(u=z_2-z_3\). Take the normal test function \(u\chi(u)\), where \(\chi\) is smooth, compactly supported and equal to one near zero. Since \(r_2=-\pi\partial_u\delta_{\mathbb C}\,d\bar u\), the derivative of the test at zero gives \(+\pi\hbar\) when the remaining field and tangent factors are paired to one. A correction supported at equal heights cannot cancel this reading.

theorems.title: Theorem — radial circuit transport
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem — radial circuit transport.** Let \(\mathscr S\) be the span of the complete first and successive circuit contacts, their stated spectator compositions, smooth form multiples and finite holomorphic derivatives. On \(\mathscr S\) the positive-scale pullback has a unique continuous joint-current extension to zero. It extends as a chain family to
\(\mathscr V=\mathscr S+d_F\mathscr S\). Its proper parameter integral gives

\[
H_F(\alpha,\gamma)=(h\alpha,-h\gamma),\qquad
h=\int_0^1\iota_{\partial_\lambda}\mathcal P\,d\lambda,
\]

\[
d_FH_F+H_Fd_F=\operatorname{id}-\operatorname{sp}_0.
\]

Both endpoints and the homotopy take values in the original ambient relative current complex with the same \(Z\). The three successive contact branches retain their full sum-zero relation, including unmatched fields, vacuum terms and all finite normal jets.

theorems.title: Counterexample (a second height derivative)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Counterexample (a second height derivative).** Take the whole kernel \(K_t=[b_1(t,v)^2]\) with no independent height in the test. Pair its symmetric second difference quotient \((K_t+K_{-t}-2K_0)/t^2\) with \(v^2\chi(|v|^2)\), for a smooth compact cutoff equal to one near zero. At \(\rho=|v|\) the two linear terms in \(t/\sqrt{t^2+\rho^2}\) cancel. The radial profile that remains is

\[
\frac{1}{2(t^2+\rho^2)}.
\]

With planar area measure the integral near zero is \(2\pi\int_0^{\rho_0}\rho\,d\rho/[2(t^2+\rho^2)]=\pi\log(1/|t|)+O(1)\) for fixed \(\rho_0>0\). Thus a general \(C^2\) trace without a retained real normal is false.

theorems.title: Theorem (transport of the two-mark contact)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (transport of the two-mark contact).** Adjoin \(U\), its smooth multiples, finite holomorphic derivatives and full \(d_F\)-descendants to \(\mathscr V\). The continuous cylinder limit on this larger space respects relations of joint currents because it is the ordinary pullback at every positive \(\lambda\). Applying Stokes on \([\epsilon,1]\) and passing to the limit recovers \(d_FH_F+H_Fd_F=1-\operatorname{sp}_0\) in the same fixed relative recipient. Any further disjoint spectator made solely of \(W\)'s and their finite holomorphic jets can be appended to this sector. Its only possible contractions would need an unmatched \(J\), so its product with this contact only adjoins the new particles and takes their graded symmetrization.

theorems.title: Proposition (Gaussian transport between profiles)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (Gaussian transport between profiles).** For a bounded chain isomorphism \(T\), write \(Q_T=T^*\Pi_b-\Pi_a\) for the difference of the two primitives on source fields. If \(T^*c_b=c_a\), the map that transports the quantum product and differential is

\[
\begin{aligned}
G_T&=E_b^{-1}\operatorname{Sym}(T)E_a\\
   &=\operatorname{Sym}(T)\exp\!\bigl(-\partial_{Q_T}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

theorems.title: Example (The first descendant in a four-point block)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Return to the circle around \(0,z\). Place primary fields of weights \(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4\) at \(0,z,1,\infty\), respectively, and keep a positive intermediate label of weight \(h\). Divide out the two trivalent constants so that each primary coefficient at unit separation is one. What is the first correction to propagation of the intermediate highest state? The inner primary amplitude is \(z^{h-h_1-h_2}\). To test the level-one state \(L_{-1}\Omega\) on the seam, move its transpose \(L_1\) onto the primary at \(z\). Its Ward action \(z^2\partial_z+2h_2 z\) gives
\[
 (z^2\partial_z+2h_2z)z^{h-h_1-h_2}
   =(h+h_2-h_1)z^{h-h_1-h_2+1}.
\]
On the outer disk the primary amplitude with the third field at \(y\) is \(y^{h_4-h-h_3}\). Translating the seam insertion while holding \(y\) fixed gives minus the \(y\)-derivative, hence \(h+h_3-h_4\) at \(y=1\). The two linear functionals compose through the inverse Gram entry \(1/(2h)\). The resulting block starts with
\[
 z^{h-h_1-h_2}\left(1+
  \frac{(h+h_2-h_1)(h+h_3-h_4)}{2h}\,z+O(z^2)\right).
\]
For four equal external weights the relative coefficient is \(h/2\). At \(c=25\) and intermediate momentum \(1/2\) it is \(5/8\). This number is a coefficient at one fixed momentum. A comparison between cuts also uses the higher levels and the dependence on momentum. [Al. B. Zamolodchikov, *An Explicit Recurrence Formula for the Conformal Partial Wave Amplitude*, equations (1)–(3)](https://strings.itp.ac.ru/Papers/zamolodchikov1984.pdf#page=1).

theorems.title: Theorem 10.1 (finite analytic sewing)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Under the normalized boundary hypothesis and the two-radius estimates above, fix \(d\ge2\), \(s\in\mathbb R\), positive external labels, and

\[
K\Subset\{0<|a_2|<\cdots<|a_d|,\;
                              s<-\log|a_d|\}
\]

on a logarithmic coordinate cover. There is a finite input exponent \(t_K\) for which the actual left-associated sewing is a holomorphic Hilbert–Schmidt family

\[
C_d(\mathbf a):\mathcal H_{\mathbf p}[t_K]\longrightarrow\mathcal Z_d[s].
\]

It therefore acts continuously on \(E_{\mathbf p}\). Every internal and output spectrum and every descendant level is uncut. Cutoffs in input, intermediate and output levels, and in the momenta, converge in Hilbert–Schmidt norm uniformly on smaller compact sets. The scalar factor is exactly

\[
2^{(d-1)/4}\sqrt{\prod_{v}C_0(k_{v,L},k_{v,R},k_v)},
\]

with one factor for each binary vertex. Bounds are uniform in the external positive labels and locally uniform in \(c\). They need not be uniform in \(d\), near collisions, or at the boundary of the strict output inequality. [*Radial comb sewings*, Theorem FC.3](#ref-ch10-01) · [Finite radial combs under the boundary hypothesis](#atlas-c-analytic-all-finite-radial-combs).

theorems.title: Theorem 10.2 (intrinsic complete sources)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 10.2 (intrinsic complete sources).** With the elementary outputs and topologies above, retain the normalized four-point data, the energy estimates and the prescribed vacuum graph bounds. Then \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{com}}(R)\) is complete and Hausdorff and injects continuously and densely into \(R\). Every continuous Virasoro map restricts continuously to these sources. Meromorphic vector-field germs with finite principal part act by absolutely convergent mode series. On the elementary positive and vacuum objects the construction recovers the original topology exactly; in particular,

\[
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{com}}(R_p)
 =\mathscr E_p,
\qquad
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{com}}(V(M))
 =M\widehat\otimes_\pi G.
\]

An arbitrary common source need not be metrizable or nuclear. [*Complete functorial sources extending the original inputs*, Theorems IS.1–IS.4](#ref-ch10-08).

theorems.title: Proposition (descent through a sewn image)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (descent through a sewn image).** Fix a finite sewing \(\mu:E\to R\) on its complete Fréchet input at a fixed configuration, with \(R\) its specified complete Hausdorff recipient. The sewn vector determines the factorization
\[
E\xrightarrow{\pi}T=E/\ker\mu
\xrightarrow{\,j\,}\overline{\mu(E)}^{\,R},
\qquad j([v])=\mu(v).
\]
The kernel is closed because \(\mu\) is continuous and \(R\) is Hausdorff, so \(T\) is complete Fréchet. The quotient remembers which preparations are equivalent. Its map \(j\) identifies these classes as a set with the sewn vectors. The same image also has the topology inherited from \(R\). An outer operation defined on the closure must be continuous for this latter topology. In particular, whenever sewn vectors \(\mu(v_\alpha)\) tend to zero in \(R\), their assigned values must tend to zero in the next recipient, regardless of how the preparations \(v_\alpha\) behave in \(E\). For a continuous linear map \(F:E\to W\) to factor through the completed image, two conditions enter.

1. It must annihilate the actual kernel, \(F(\ker\mu)=0\), so that its value depends only on the sewn vector.
2. The induced map on \(\mu(E)\) must be continuous for the topology inherited from \(R\), if it is to extend continuously to the completed image in \(R\).

For complete Hausdorff \(W\), these conditions give the unique continuous extension from the dense image.

theorems.title: Injectivity of the fixed-label positive radial comb
theorems.statement_excerpt: Fix \(c>1\), \(d\ge2\) and positive external momenta \(\mathbf p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\). Take \(a_1=0\), \(0<|a_2|<\cdots<|a_d|\) on the logarithmic cover, and \(s<-\log|a_d|\). Under the normalized four-point hypothesis, the every-fibre two-radius and cutoff estimates of Theorem 10.1, and the full rational Ward identity with its convergent regular input germs, the actual map \(C_d(\mathbf a):E_{\mathbf p}\to\mathcal Z_d[s]\) is injective. The same holds for its tree continuations on the compatible lifts.

theorems.title: Two independently completed conformal blocks
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Put the outer separation equal to one. For \(s<0\), take \(r>\log 2\) and \(t>\log 2\) sufficiently large on the moving leg for the two-radius estimate. Take two independent inputs on the corresponding graphs with positive sections \(f(p),g(q)\). Under the normalized boundary hypothesis the two continuous outputs on their completed projective tensor product are

\[
\begin{aligned}
 (p,q,e)&\longmapsto\mu_{p,q}(1)(f(p),g(q))(e)
   &&\text{in }L^2(d\nu(p)d\nu(q)d\nu(e);H_e[s]),\\
 p&\longmapsto\beta_{p,p}(1)(f(p),g(p))
   &&\text{in }V(L^2(d\nu)).
\end{aligned}
\]

Here \(\beta_{p,p}\) is the bilinear three-point vacuum block with value one on its three highest vectors. The positive-channel norm integrates over the two independent momenta using the Gaussian bound. For the vacuum channel the output is still a function of \(p\). In the product measure \(d\nu(p)d\nu(q)\), the diagonal contraction has density \(\delta(p-q)/m_{\mathfrak b}(q)\). Integrating first over \(q\) cancels its density \(m_{\mathfrak b}(q)\) and evaluates the second section at \(p\). The annular estimate bounds its resolved Hilbert norm by \(C\|e^{rE}f\|_\infty\|e^{tE}g\|_2\).

theorems.title: A resolved vacuum output with weighted Hilbert inputs
theorems.statement_excerpt: Keep the labels, normalization, outer vertex and exponents \(r,t\) of the preceding two-cluster result. Choose fixed nonzero logarithmic inner coordinates with \(r<-\log|\zeta_1|\) and \(t<-\log|\zeta_2|\). Give each input the topology of its full marked tuple together with just the weighted \(L^2(d\nu)\) norm of its positive section. There are inputs tending to zero in these topologies whose vacuum ground outputs have unbounded \(L^2(d\nu)\) norm in the retained momentum. The resolved vacuum operation has no continuous bilinear extension to these weakened graphs agreeing on the original preparations.

theorems.title: Example (the vacuum stress coefficient)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (the vacuum stress coefficient).** Take \(\mathfrak b=2^{-1/4}\), \(a=1\), \(b=2\), and two highest-state pairs at the same small positive inner separation \(\tau\). Multiply each pair's input by \(\tau^{2h_i}\), \(i=a,b\), to give its vacuum ground coefficient one. Its pairing with \(L_{-n}\Omega\) is \((n-1)h_i\tau^n\) for every \(n\ge2\). At \(w=1/2\) the physical vacuum coefficient in either expansion is
\[
 (96+12\sqrt2)\tau^2-192\tau^3+O(\tau^4).
\]
The level-two vector \((2h_i/c)\tau^2L_{-2}\Omega\) pairs with the stress two-point function \(c/(2w^4)\) at the first centre and \(c/(2(w-1)^4)\) at the second. Together these give \(16(h_a+h_b)\tau^2\). The level-three translations differentiate at the two opposite centres. Their opposite signs give \(64(h_a-h_b)\tau^3\).

theorems.title: Example (Two fillings with the same boundary amplitude)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Now couple the interior coordinate to the boundary. Keep the oriented coordinates \(x,y\) and their Lebesgue densities fixed. For a real coupling \(b\), prepare the action \(S_b(x,y)=\tfrac12\lambda x^2+\tfrac12\mu(y-bx)^2\). Integrating at fixed \(x\) produces the boundary amplitude
\[
 A_b(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-S_b(x,y)/\hbar}\,dy
        =\sqrt{2\pi\hbar/\mu}\,e^{-\lambda x^2/(2\hbar)} .
\]
The substitution \(y'=y-bx\) has unit Jacobian. Thus even the absolute amplitude \(A_b(x)\) is independent of \(b\). For example, a second filling with amplitude \(e^{-\lambda' x^2/(2\hbar)}\), \(\lambda'>0\), gives the same sewn vacuum \(2\pi\hbar/\sqrt{\mu(\lambda+\lambda')}\) for every \(b\) when we integrate the product against \(dx\). In the original filling the specified interior coordinate \(y\) has conditional mean \(bx\) at fixed \(x\). Therefore \(\langle xy\rangle_b=b\langle x^2\rangle_b=b\hbar/\lambda\). The two fillings with couplings \(b\) and \(-b\), \(b\ne0\), agree on every insertion at the cut and give opposite expectations for this mixed insertion. The coordinate reflection that exchanges their actions also reverses the specified interior probe. To compare the fillings on bulk observables one must say how the probe is identified.

theorems.title: A mixed measurement separates states with identical mode marginals
theorems.statement_excerpt:
On the half-space take the closed cycles \(i_\hbar I_B((p_1^2\pm p_2)/2)\). On the disk take the two amplitudes \(F_\pm=(Z_1^2\pm Z_2)/2\) and measure the real, rotation-invariant function of the central field derivatives

\[
C=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(h'(0)^2\overline{h''(0)}\bigr)
  =Z_1^2\bar Z_2+\bar Z_1^2Z_2 .
\]

Its operator on holomorphic states is the Toeplitz operator \(T_C\), multiplication by \(C\) followed by orthogonal projection. Gaussian integration by parts turns \(\bar Z_n\) under this projection into \(n\partial_{Z_n}\). The two indices in each term are distinct, so \(T_C=VOV^{-1}\) on polynomials. The vectors \(p_1^2,p_2\) are orthogonal and each has squared norm two. On their span write \(S\) for the operator exchanging the unit vectors \(p_1^2/\sqrt2\) and \(p_2/\sqrt2\). Then \(O=2S\), and the two prepared states are norm-one eigenvectors of \(S\) with eigenvalues \(\pm1\). Under the unitary \(V\) the Fock-space calculation gives \(\langle F_\pm,T_CF_\pm\rangle=\pm2\).

The disk probabilities give a direct check of what is measured. Put \(x=Z_1=h'(0)\) and \(y=Z_2=h''(0)\). Under the vacuum law \(\mu\) these are independent circular complex Gaussians with \(\mathbb E_\mu|x|^2=1\) and \(\mathbb E_\mu|y|^2=2\). The two preparations have densities relative to \(\mu\)
\[
 |F_\pm|^2=\tfrac14|x^2\pm y|^2
 =\tfrac14(|x|^4+|y|^2)\ \pm\ \tfrac12\operatorname{Re}(x^2\bar y).
\]
Their difference is \(R=\operatorname{Re}(x^2\bar y)\). It integrates to zero at fixed \(x\) by the circular symmetry of \(y\), and at fixed \(y\) by that of \(x\). Thus the two marginal distributions agree for each mode. To test the joint distribution, observe that \(x^2\bar y\) is circular and \(\mathbb E_\mu|x|^4=2\). Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_\mu R^2=\tfrac12\mathbb E_\mu|x|^4\,\mathbb E_\mu|y|^2=2.
\]
The term \(R(|x|^4+|y|^2)\) has zero expectation by symmetry. The joint observable \(C=2R\) therefore has mean \(+2\) in \(|F_+|^2d\mu\) and \(-2\) in \(|F_-|^2d\mu\). A single measurement gives the value \(2\operatorname{Re}(x^2\bar y)\) for that filling, which varies with both boundary modes.

::: example {#ch11-squaring-the-disk-reading title="Squaring a reading on the disk"}

What does performing the boundary operation twice correspond to on the disk? Let \(\Pi\) project orthogonally onto holomorphic amplitudes. The operator \(T_C^2\) includes a projection between the two multiplications by \(C\), and \(T_C^2F_\pm=4F_\pm\). Squaring the number recorded on one filling uses the pointwise function \(C^2\). At fixed \(|x|,|y|\) its vacuum angular average is \(2|x|^4|y|^2\), and the term odd in \(R\) integrates to zero. Thus in each preparation
\[
 \int C^2 |F_\pm|^2\,d\mu
  =\tfrac12\left(\mathbb E_\mu|x|^8\,\mathbb E_\mu|y|^2+
                  \mathbb E_\mu|x|^4\,\mathbb E_\mu|y|^4\right)
  =\tfrac12(24\cdot2+2\cdot8)=32 .
\]
The variance of the dimensionless disk reading is \(32-4=28\). On these polynomials the difference between the two second moments is exactly \(\|(1-\Pi)CF_\pm\|^2\). This component leaves the holomorphic space after the first multiplication and is removed by the projection before the second boundary operation.

:::

Both amplitudes have oscillator grade two. Inserting a cylinder on one side of the field measurement propagates the holomorphic state after \(T_C\) has acted. The **one-sided** collar pairing and its normalization are consequently

\[
\langle F_\pm,P_qT_CF_\pm\rangle=\pm2q^2,\qquad
\langle F_\pm,P_qF_\pm\rangle=q^2 .
\]

theorems.title: Proposition (density waves of free fermions)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (density waves of free fermions).** Let \(p^\alpha=\prod_np_n^{\alpha_n}\) and \(p^\beta=\prod_np_n^{\beta_n}\) be monomials of energies \(\sum_nn\alpha_n\le N\) and \(\sum_nn\beta_n\le N\). Then
\[
\int p^\alpha(x)\,\overline{p^\beta(x)}\,d\nu_N(x)
=\delta_{\alpha\beta}\prod_{n\ge1}n^{\alpha_n}\alpha_n!
=\mathbb E_\mu\bigl[Z^\alpha\,\overline{Z^\beta}\bigr].
\]
In particular the substitution \(F\mapsto F(p(x))\,\psi_0\) preserves the inner product on the span of the occupation monomials of weighted degree at most \(N\).

theorems.title: Proposition (kinetic energy in the density waves)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (kinetic energy in the density waves).** For every polynomial \(F\),
\[
\sum_{a=1}^ND_a^2\,\bigl(F(p(x))\,\psi_0\bigr)
=\bigl((2W+NE+c_N)F\bigr)(p(x))\,\psi_0,
\qquad c_N=\frac{N(N^2-1)}{12}.
\]
Consequently \(K\) acts on these states as \(K_0+\varepsilon_1\bigl(E+\tfrac2NW\bigr)\). Here \(K_0\) is the energy of the ground state and \(\varepsilon_1=(\hbar^2/2m)(2\pi/L)^2N=2\pi\hbar v_F/L\), with \(v_F=\pi\hbar N/(mL)\) the slope of the kinetic energy halfway between the highest occupied momentum \(\pi\hbar(N-1)/L\) and the next allowed momentum \(\pi\hbar(N+1)/L\). Since the kinetic energy is quadratic, raising the last fermion by one step costs exactly \(\varepsilon_1\). At fixed density \(N/L\), the velocities at both momenta tend to \(v_F\) as \(L\) grows.

theorems.title: Theorem (the spectrum of the cubic observable)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (the spectrum of the cubic observable).** Let \(\lambda\) be a partition of \(n\), and let \(s_\lambda\) be the polynomial in \(p_1,\ldots,p_n\) which becomes the Schur polynomial \(s_\lambda(x)\) in any number \(N\ge n\) of variables. Then
\[
W\,s_\lambda=c(\lambda)\,s_\lambda,\qquad
c(\lambda)=\sum_{(i,j)\in\lambda}(j-i)=\frac12\sum_i\lambda_i(\lambda_i-2i+1),
\]
where \((i,j)\) runs over the boxes of the Young diagram of \(\lambda\), in row \(i\) and column \(j\). The \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\) a partition of \(n\) form an orthonormal basis of the states of energy \(n\). On that space \(W\) is symmetric, with norm \(n(n-1)/2\).

theorems.title: Proposition (the momenta are a complete measurement)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Proposition (the momenta are a complete measurement).** The sequence \(M_1(\lambda),M_2(\lambda),M_3(\lambda),\ldots\) determines the partition \(\lambda\).

theorems.title: Theorem (the cubic observable on the disk)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (the cubic observable on the disk).** For a unit vector \(F\) supported on finitely many oscillator grades,
\[
\int\Phi_r\,|F(Z)|^2\,d\mu=\langle F,W_rF\rangle\longrightarrow\langle F,WF\rangle\qquad(r\uparrow1).
\]
More generally let \(\rho\) be a positive trace-class operator of trace one on the completed Fock space. If \(\rho=\sum_j\lambda_j|F_j\rangle\langle F_j|\) in unit eigenvectors, its disk law is \(d\nu_\rho=\sum_j\lambda_j|F_j(Z)|^2d\mu\). A real collar acting on both sides, with \(0<q<1\), prepares \(\rho_q=q^E\rho\,q^E/\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\,q^{2E})\). Then \(\Phi_r\) is integrable for the law \(\nu_{\rho_q}\) of the state \(\rho_q\), and
\[
\lim_{r\uparrow1}\int\Phi_r\,d\nu_{\rho_q}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_qW).
\]
In particular \(\int\Phi_r\,|F_\pm|^2\,d\mu=\pm r^4\).

theorems.title: Proposition (boundary fluctuations of the cubic disk observable)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (boundary fluctuations of the cubic disk observable).** Take \(\Phi_r,\Phi_s\) on the same filling, at radii \(0<r,s<1\). Under the vacuum law \(\mu\) they have mean zero and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_\mu(\Phi_r,\Phi_s)
 =\frac{2x^2(1+x)}{(1-x)^5},\qquad x=(rs)^2 .
\]
{#eq-cubic-disk-covariance}
For every fixed probability law \(\nu\) absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\), and every fixed \(H>0\),
\[
 \lim_{r\uparrow1}\ \sup_{a\in\mathbb R}
       \nu\bigl(|\Phi_r-a|\le H\bigr)=0 .
\]
{#eq-cubic-disk-escape}

theorems.title: Theorem (recovering a density operator from its filling law)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (recovering a density operator from its filling law).** For the neutral free current at level one on the marked disk, the map \(\rho\mapsto\nu_\rho\) is injective on positive trace-class operators of trace one. Each finite set of harmonics determines a reduced density operator. Taking successively more harmonics recovers the matrix entries of \(\rho\).

theorems.title: Theorem (the ratio determines a known shell)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (the ratio determines a known shell).** Let \(K\) be a nonnegative integer, and let \(\rho\) be a density operator on the states of oscillator grade \(K\) of the first two harmonics, which are spanned by \(p_1^{K-2j}p_2^{\,j}\) for \(0\le j\le K/2\). Suppose the two transmissions are known and positive. Then the probability law of the single complex number \(Z_2/Z_1^2\) determines \(\rho\).

theorems.title: A neutral level-one ray pair and a sourced disk at finite radius
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Each of the first \(N\) means shifts to \(ar^n\) and its variance remains \(n\). For \(M\le N\), the disk inner product of \(e^{ah_M(r)}\) and \(e^{ah_N(r)}\) is \(e^{a^2L_M}\), by independence of the tail. The squared distance is therefore \(e^{a^2L_N}-e^{a^2L_M}\). The exponentials converge in the holomorphic Hilbert space, and their normalized squared moduli converge in \(L^1(\mu)\). The ray state has squared norm \(r^{-2a^2}(1-r^2)^{-a^2}\). Its normalized harmonic filling law is exactly \(e^{2a\operatorname{Re}h(r)-a^2L}\,d\mu\).

The disk source fixes a probability law. Put \(L=-\log(1-r^2)\) and \(L_q=-\log(1-qr^2)\). Relative to \(\mu\), the positive square root of its density is \(e^{a\operatorname{Re}h(r)-a^2L/2}\). The normalised ray has holomorphic amplitude \(e^{a h(r)-a^2L/2}\). These amplitudes have identical squared moduli. Their matrix elements under a collar can differ. The two real parts of \(h(r)\) at the ends of the vacuum Mehler collar have variance \(L/2\) each and covariance \(L_q/2\). The normalised collar pairing of the positive square root is therefore \(\exp[a^2(L_q-L)/2]\). Requiring a holomorphic amplitude selects the ray state up to phase by the [disk reconstruction theorem](#ch11-recovering-a-state-from-the-disk).

The real collar sends each oscillator \(p_n\) in the second amplitude to \(q^n p_n\). Its exponential therefore contains \((qr)^n\), while the endpoint contraction still contributes \(r^{-a^2}\) to each amplitude. Pairing the two exponentials inserts \(qr^2\) into the covariance sum. With \(V\) the Fock-to-disk isometry, this gives

\[
\frac{\langle V\Psi_{a,r},P_q V\Psi_{a,r}\rangle}
     {\|V\Psi_{a,r}\|^2}
=\exp\!\left(a^2\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(q^n-1)r^{2n}}{n}\right)
=\left(\frac{1-r^2}{1-qr^2}\right)^{a^2}.
\]

At zero collar length \(q=1\), the numerator is the squared norm \(r^{-2a^2}(1-r^2)^{-a^2}\). At zero charge the state is the vacuum for every collar. In both cases the ratio is one. At fixed \(r\), multiplying the ray vector by any scalar \(c(r)\ne0\) multiplies its squared norm, the disk weight \(|V\Psi_{a,r}|^2\) and the collar numerator by \(|c(r)|^2\). Thus the mutual ray factor \(r^{-a^2}\) enters both normalized readings through its squared modulus \(r^{-2a^2}\), which cancels. For nonzero real \(a\) the unnormalized norm diverges as \(r\uparrow1\). Neutrality places the output in the disk theory with its constant mode fixed to zero. A nonneutral output requires a charged zero-mode sector.

Keep the framing and outgoing subtraction fixed and move the endpoint of charge \(a\) from \(r\) to \(s\), with \(0<s<1\). The disk means change from \(ar^n\) to \(as^n\). The ray contraction multiplies the vacuum coefficient by \((s/r)^{-a^2}\). A filling with the same normalized disk law must also reproduce this factor to agree on the ray amplitude. For an [absolute cap comparison](17-holographic-reconstruction.md#states-lines-and-caps), the filling must supply its own amplitude \(Z(1)\) with no insertion. After the two vacuum lines are identified, their nonzero empty-insertion amplitudes must agree. One must also show that pairing the boundary states along the cut gives the amplitude of the glued filling.

For \(M\le N\), the disk inner product of \(e^{ah_M(r)}\) and \(e^{ah_N(r)}\) is \(e^{a^2L_M}\), by independence of the tail. The squared distance is therefore \(e^{a^2L_N}-e^{a^2L_M}\). The exponentials converge in the holomorphic Hilbert space, and their normalized squared moduli converge in \(L^1(\mu)\). The ray state has squared norm \(r^{-2a^2}(1-r^2)^{-a^2}\). Its normalized harmonic filling law is exactly \(e^{2a\operatorname{Re}h(r)-a^2L}\,d\mu\).

theorems.title: Theorem 11.1 (normalized numerical Gaussian)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 11.1 (normalized numerical Gaussian).** Fix the original metric and density, \(0<|q|<1\), \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\hbar>0\), and a smooth integrable \(\mu\) with zero normal trace in the single small \(C^1\) inverse neighbourhood. Supply a smooth solution \(T_\mu\) of the Ward equation above, based by \(T_0=0\) for families through zero. Exhaust the singular pairs by increasing finite windows. For each pair in even degree choose one circular complex Gaussian \(w_{j,\ell}\) with \(\mathbb E|w_{j,\ell}|^2=\hbar\), independently over pairs, and use that same variable in every window containing the pair. The resulting fields \(\Phi_{\Lambda,\mu}\) converge in mean square and almost surely in \(\mathscr D_{-6}\) to a centered Radon Gaussian \(\Phi_\mu\). Its law has support equal to the closure of \(\mathfrak A_\mu\mathsf W\). Let \(P_\Lambda\) project onto the retained real and imaginary singular-pair coordinates in \(\mathsf W\). In their orthonormal coordinate basis \(e_n\),

\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathbb E\|\Phi_\mu-\Phi_{\Lambda,\mu}\|_{-6}^2
=\frac{\hbar}{2}\|\mathfrak A_\mu(1-P_\Lambda)\|_{\rm HS}^2\\
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
 \sum_{P_\Lambda e_n=0}\|\mathfrak A_\mu e_n\|_{-6}^2
\longrightarrow0 .
\end{gathered}
\]

Each real coordinate of \(w_{j,\ell}\) has variance \(\hbar/2\). The sum in the display is the tail of the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm. Orthogonality of the independent increments gives the mean-square limit, and the Hilbert-valued Gaussian series converges almost surely. The real covariance is
\(\frac{\hbar}{2}\mathfrak A_\mu\mathfrak A_\mu^*\), with the real Hilbert adjoint. Odd and mixed moments converge by the graded Wick rule for the full inverse action. They do not define an odd-variable probability measure. Parameter-uniform statements require bounds on the finitely many higher source and background seminorms used in the estimates. [*A numerical Gaussian on the native source graph*, Theorems 4–6](#ref-ch11-01).

theorems.title: Theorem 11.2 (original heat finite part)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem 11.2 (original heat finite part).** Use the original fixed-adjoint weighted realization above, with smooth reflected \(\mu,T\) sufficiently small in \(\|\mu\|_{C^4}+\|T\|_{C^1}\) and the stated bounds on higher seminorms. Put \(\ell_q=-\log|q|\). The coefficient supertrace on the reflection-even sector has, for every \(0<\delta<1/2\),

\[
\tau_+(t,u)=\operatorname{Str}_{X}(Ne^{-tA_+(u)})
=-\frac{\ell_q}{4t}+\frac{B(u)}{\sqrt t}+C(u)+O(t^\delta),
\]

where \(B(u),C(u)\) are scalar local heat coefficients. The estimate holds after each specified finite number of source derivatives under the higher-seminorm bounds. The coefficient of \(t^0\log t\) is zero. Consequently, with

\[
W_\epsilon(u)=-\int_\epsilon^\infty\tau_+(t,u)\frac{dt}{t},
\qquad
D_\epsilon(u)=\frac{\ell_q}{4\epsilon}
 -\frac{2B(u)}{\sqrt\epsilon}+C(u)\log\epsilon,
\]

the finite part \(W_{\mathrm{fp}}=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}(W_\epsilon-D_\epsilon)\) exists with error \(O_{C^k}(\epsilon^\delta)\). It is holomorphic on the admitted holomorphic source families. [*The original coefficient heat finite part and its based vacuum line*, Theorems 3–4](#ref-ch11-04).

theorems.title: Theorem (coproducts on a fixed weighted polynomial algebra)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (coproducts on a fixed weighted polynomial algebra).** Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic zero. Give \(A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n,z]\) the augmentation at the origin, with \(x_i\) of weight one and \(z\) of weight two. All generators have cohomological degree zero and the differential vanishes. The connected graded Hopf structures on \(A\) have exactly \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\) graded Hopf isomorphism classes. Each \(x_i\) is primitive. Writing \(u_i=x_i\otimes1\) and \(v_i=1\otimes x_i\), the remaining formulas are
\[
\Delta_B z=z\otimes1+1\otimes z+B(u,v),\qquad
S_B x_i=-x_i,\quad S_B z=-z+B(x,x),
\]
where \(B(u,v)=u^{\mathsf t}Bv\) is any bilinear form. The isomorphism class is determined by the rank of \(\omega=B-B^{\mathsf t}\).

theorems.title: Example (primitive fields at two levels)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (primitive fields at two levels).** Over \(R=k\), fix \(c\in k\) and take \(H=k[x_0,x_1,\ldots]\) with each \(x_n\) primitive, \(Tx_n=x_{n+1}\), and \(\rho_z(x_m,x_n)=(-1)^n\partial_z^{m+n}(c/z)\). The two product rules extend this kernel to the polynomial algebra. For the identity level the three terms of the iterated coproduct of \(x_0\) give \(\delta_{\mathrm{id}}(x_0)=x_0\otimes1\). For the level \(\eta x_n=-x_n\) they give \(\delta_\eta(x_0)=x_0\otimes1+1\otimes2x_0\). Substitution into the field formula gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_{\mathrm{id}}(x_0,z)x_0&=x_0(z)x_0,\\
Y_\eta(x_0,z)x_0&=x_0(z)x_0-\frac{2c}{z}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The sign comes from evaluating the contraction at \(-z\). On this cocommutative Hopf algebra the identity-level coaction is \(b\mapsto b\otimes1\) for every \(b\). All its identity-level fields are therefore independent of \(c\). On the pair of regular comodules with coaction \(\Delta\), interchanging \(x_0\otimes x_0\) adds \(-c\,1\otimes1/z\) to the flipped tensor. The pair of regular comodules therefore distinguishes two values of \(c\) even when the identity-level field algebras coincide. [CQ2](#ref-ch12-cq2)

theorems.title: Theorem (spectral field and coproduct construction)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (spectral field and coproduct construction).** Under the hypotheses above, \(V_\eta\) is a quantum vertex algebra with vacuum \(1\), translation \(T\), and rational exchange
\[
\mathcal S_\eta(z)(a\otimes b)
=a_{(0)}\otimes b_{(0)}\rho_z(a_{(1)},b_{(1)}).
\]
Every finite ordered product on a fixed state has a common finite denominator. For \(V_1=V_{\eta_1}\) and \(V_2=V_{\eta_2}\), their tensor product \(\boxtimes_\rho\) has underlying module \(V_1\otimes_RV_2\) with right coaction
\[
\delta_{12}(c\otimes d)
=c_{(0)}\otimes d_{(0)}\otimes d_{(1)}c_{(1)}.
\]
The second state's \(H\)-component multiplies the first on the left. The usual tensor product of right comodules would give \(c_{(1)}d_{(1)}\) in the last slot. The fields are
\[
Y_{12}(a\otimes b,z)(c\otimes d)
=Y_1(a,z)c_{(0)}\otimes Y_2(b_{(0)},z)d\,
\rho_{-z}(c_{(1)},b_{(1)}).
\]
The maps
\[
D_{\eta_1,\eta_2}=(\eta_2\otimes1)\Delta:
V_{\eta_1\eta_2}\longrightarrow
V_{\eta_1}\boxtimes_\rho V_{\eta_2}
\]
preserve fields, vacuum, translation and coaction. They are coassociative, with counit \(\varepsilon:V_{\mathrm{id}}\to R\) at the identity level. They induce maps of residue coalgebras and their augmented associative chiral cobars. Over a field, the same constructions descend to the ordered collision schemes. [CQ2](#ref-ch12-cq2)

theorems.title: Spin intertwiners and the oriented Ising half-turn
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Gluing two channels sums over a **common** intermediate label \(j\). On \(v\otimes w\), the projector is \(\sum_j ve_j\otimes e_j w\). Thus a mismatched pair of channels vanishes, even when both channel vectors are nonzero. Composition of these maps with the fusion associator therefore identifies \(\mathcal F(M)\otimes_A\mathcal F(N)\) with \(\mathcal F(M\boxtimes N)\). Their complex vector-space dimensions on \(\mathbf1,\psi,\sigma\) are \(3,3,4\). The reconstructed algebra is a ribbon weak Hopf algebra \(H\) of dimension \(3^2+3^2+4^2=34\). Its coproduct on the unit, \(\Delta(1)\), projects the ordinary tensor product onto the pairs with matching intermediate labels. This is the space on which exchange acts. [Matching endpoints](02-algebras-and-modules.md#ch02-ising-matching-ends) · [CQ9](#ref-ch12-cq9)

For three input spins with total output \(\sigma\), the first two can fuse through \(\mathbf1\) or through \(\psi\). Either channel can then fuse with the third spin to give \(\sigma\). Keep these two paths as the basis for the exchange. The two basis vectors correspond to \((\sigma\sigma)_{\mathbf1}\sigma\) and \((\sigma\sigma)_\psi\sigma\). A half-turn here means positive analytic continuation of the two insertions through angle \(\pi\) in the marked chiral blocks. In the real trivalent basis, with \(\zeta=e^{\pi i/8}\), the positive half-turn of the first pair and the change of fusion channel have matrices

\[
B_1=\begin{pmatrix}\zeta^{-1}&0\\0&\zeta^3\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
F=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Removing the scalar \(\zeta^{-2}\) from \(B_1^2\) gives \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\). For the second pair it gives \(FZF=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The two involutions anticommute and their products span the full two-by-two matrix algebra. More generally the complex algebra generated by adjacent double exchanges on \(\sigma^{\boxtimes n}\) is its entire intertwiner algebra. For instance four spins have two vacuum paths and two fermion paths, giving \(M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus M_2(\mathbb C)\). This assertion takes linear combinations of braids. In each simple output of multiplicity \(d\), individual pure braids have only \(d^2\) projective images.

Reflection inverts both half-turn phases. Their **labelled ratio** in the fermion and vacuum channels changes from \(i\) to \(-i\), while both squared phases acquire the same factor \(i\). Thus projective double exchanges lose the orientation. The twist of a framed spin, \(\zeta\) in the given orientation and \(\zeta^{-1}\) in the mirror, also distinguishes them. For the [Gaussian rays](11-states-and-lines.md#ch11-neutral-ray-pair) the channel is one dimensional. At level \(k\ne0\) the operation on charges \(a,b\) has coefficient \(z^{ab/k}\), continued from the positive real branch. The upper half-turn \(z\mapsto e^{\pi i}z\) multiplies it by \(e^{\pi iab/k}\). Parallel transport on the dual state line has the inverse factor. For \(a=b=1,\ k=2\), the operation acquires \(i\), the dual acquires \(-i\), and their evaluation has factor \(1\). The exponent \(1/2\) requires a branch even though the evaluated scalar is single-valued. [CQ9](#ref-ch12-cq9), [CQ10](#ref-ch12-cq10)

theorems.title: Proposition (ordered spectral cuts)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (ordered spectral cuts).** Attach a spectral position \(s_i\) to each of \(n\) consecutive outputs. Put \(\sigma_sg(u)=g(u+s)\), \(\tau_s\xi(u)=\xi(u+s)\), \(P_0=e\) and
\[
 P_i=(\sigma_{s_1}g_1)\cdots(\sigma_{s_i}g_i).
\]
There is a polynomial family of vertex-algebra maps \(C_{\mathbf s}:V\to V^{\otimes n}[s_1,\ldots,s_n]\) given by
\[
 C_{\mathbf s}f=f(P_n),\qquad
 C_{\mathbf s}J_\xi=\sum_{i=1}^n
        J^{(i)}_{\tau_{-s_i}M_{P_{i-1}}\xi}.
\]
The coefficients of the \(i\)th current belong to the preceding factors. Cutting the \(i\)th output again at local positions \(t_{ij}\) gives the single ordered cut at positions \(s_i+t_{ij}\). A block with no outputs is evaluated by the counit.

theorems.title: Theorem (exchange of separated Hecke sheets)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (exchange of separated Hecke sheets).** Let \(a\ne b\) be two spectral positions, \(d=a-b\), and let \(G\) be a connected complex simple algebraic group. Choose a highest long-root triple \(E_\theta,H_\theta,F_\theta\) and take \(X,Y\in\operatorname{Lie}(G)\) in the orbit of \(E_\theta\). Write \(P_a(X)=\exp(X/(u-a))\) and normalize the invariant form by \(k_\theta(E_\theta,F_\theta)=1\). The opposite factorization
\[
 P_a(X)P_b(Y)=P_b(Y')P_a(X')
\]
exists if and only if \(d^2\ne k_\theta(X,Y)\), and is then unique. There the two framed, level-zero Hecke field algebras with separate tangent matter are isomorphic over the factor swap. The isomorphism intertwines their incoming currents, coordinate insertions and all their modes. Adjacent swaps satisfy the braid relation on the common domain of the two compositions. The chart map sends \((X,Y)\) in order \(a,b\) to \((Y',X')\) in order \(b,a\). The field isomorphism pulls fields on the \(b,a\) chart back to the \(a,b\) chart. On conformal-weight-zero forms with tensor factors labelled by site, this pullback is the expansion of the Abedin–Niu \(R(d)^{-1}\) at \(d=\infty\), with graded evaluation at \(\hbar=1\). Its inverse takes weight-zero forms from order \(a,b\) to order \(b,a\) by the expansion of \(R(d)\). [Framed Hecke sheets](#ch14-cotangent-faithful-sheets)

theorems.title: Proposition
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition.** Write a Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt vector with the commuting coordinate modes on the left and the current labels in descending order,
\[
 W=x_{\alpha_1,(-m_1)}\cdots x_{\alpha_p,(-m_p)}
 (J_{e_{i_1}})_{(-n_1)}\cdots (J_{e_{i_r}})_{(-n_r)}\mathbf1,
 \qquad m_j,n_j\ge1 .
\]
Fix orders within each repeated label. If any \(m_j>1\), then \(q(W)=0\). Otherwise, with \(d=\sum_j(n_j-1)\),
\[
 q(W)=(-1)^d x_{\alpha_1}\cdots x_{\alpha_p}\,e_{i_r}\cdots e_{i_1}.
\]
Consequently the kernel has a basis consisting of all words with a differentiated coordinate and, for each remaining word with \(d>0\), the difference \(W-(-1)^d W^\flat\), where \(W^\flat\) replaces every \(n_j\) by one. At leading conformal weight the kernel is \(C_2(V)=\operatorname{span}\{a_{(-2)}b\}\), and the associated graded Zhu algebra is \(A\otimes\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak a)\) with the Poisson bracket induced by the current bracket and dressing action. [Zeng, Theorem 2.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.10202v2#S2.Thmtheorem6) · [Corollary 5.13](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.10202v2#S5.Thmtheorem13)

theorems.title: Theorem (rational affine field comparison)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (rational affine field comparison).** For every \(N\ge2\) and every \(K\in\mathbb C\), the divided determinant-one double is topologically free over \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\). Multiplication identifies it, as a module, with the \(\hbar\)-adically completed tensor product of its creation and annihilation halves. The integral divided-state fields agree with the Etingof–Kazhdan quantum affine fields on every state and on their exchange. The classical fibre of the vertex algebra of divided states is the universal affine vacuum vertex algebra \(V_K(\mathfrak{sl}_N)\), with the trace form fixing the level. [CQ4](#ref-ch12-cq4)

The associative algebra that acts on the vacuum has a different classical fibre. Let \(\mathfrak d_{\rm pol}=\mathfrak{sl}_N[t,t^{-1}]\oplus\mathbb C\mathbf c\), with central term \(m\delta_{m+n,0}\operatorname{tr}(ab)\mathbf c\) in \([at^m,bt^n]\). Then \(D_K/\hbar D_K=U(\mathfrak d_{\rm pol})/(\mathbf c-K)\). For example \(at^0\) for \(a\ne0\) survives in this algebra and annihilates the vacuum vector. The proof first establishes the Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt basis and the creation–annihilation factorization. It then identifies the annihilation matrix with the inverse of the operator matrix obtained from the coordinate coaction. To see why only one input of the scalar pairing is divided, write \(F\) for the determinant-one coordinate Hopf algebra, \(U\) for the completed creation algebra generated by the coefficients of \(\ell(v)=(L(v)-I)/\hbar\), and \(g\in F\). The pairing on \(F\widehat\otimes U\) has generator value
\[
 \beta_z(g,\ell_{ij}(v))=
 \frac{\rho_z(g,L_{ij}(v))-\delta_{ij}\varepsilon(g)}{\hbar}.
\]
The numerator is divisible by \(\hbar\). Dividing both inputs would require an additional power. For instance the coefficient of \(\Omega\) in \(\mathsf R(z)-I\) is already of order one in \(\hbar\). [CQ4](#ref-ch12-cq4)

theorems.title: The rank-two determinant-one RTT double in normalized modes modulo \(\hbar^2\)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
The negative-current lift also includes the shift of its argument by \(-K\hbar/2\). With these prescribed lifts, at rank two and **every** numerical level \(K\) there is an injective algebra homomorphism with proper image

\[
D_K/\hbar^2D_K\ \longrightarrow\ \bar M_2 .
\]

The precision is taken **after division** of the two same-half RTT relations and the centered mixed relation by \(\hbar^2\), and of each determinant defect by \(\hbar\). Thus the identities retain the constant and linear coefficients of each divided relation. Both divided determinants hold to this precision in every rank \(N\ge2\), even before identifying the local vacuum. For the determinant, the descending-column shifts give a translation of the diagonal states, which cancels their first integral trace correction. The remaining coefficient is an exchange difference whose collision residue is the ordered state product. In the mixed rank-two relation, sliding a current across both slots of its Cauchy correction keeps the spectator pole. The derivative from undoing the spectral shift cancels the central first-order correction. These computations take place inside the mode algebra. [CQ11](#ref-ch12-cq11)
theorems.source_paragraph: The negative-current lift also includes the shift of its argument by \(-K\hbar/2\). With these prescribed lifts, at rank two and **every** numerical level \(K\) there is an injective algebra homomorphism with proper image

theorems.title: Theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem.** For the RTT Yangian \(H=Y(\mathfrak{gl}_N)\), the word coalgebra \(C(H)\) factorizes across consecutive cuts. The associative chiral algebra \(A(H)=\Omega_{\rm cut}C(H)\) has a vacuum marking, a coassociative coproduct to two copies at the same positions, and a counit. For \(N\ge2\) its adjacent collision distinguishes the order of the states. Its bar admits no factorization across all subsets of the labels.

theorems.title: Theorem
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem.** These formulas give a quantum vertex algebra with polynomial exchange. Its residue coalgebra factorizes for all ordered decompositions, including \(\{1,3\}|\{2\}\). Over \(\mathbb C\) its cobar is an associative chiral algebra on the full ordered collision atlas. The Yangian coproduct is a morphism of the fields and their residue coalgebras into the joint same-position tensor specified below.

theorems.title: Theorem (Cartan twist of the rational quantum affine fields)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (Cartan twist of the rational quantum affine fields).** Let \(V_K^h\) be the divided determinant-one quantum affine vacuum algebra at level \(K\). Its two-parameter fields, on the same topologically free state module after base change, are
\[
 Y^{h,\eta}(a,z)b=e^{-\eta B(|a|,|b|)}Y^h(a,z)b,\qquad
 \mathcal S^{h,\eta}(z)=F_{12}\mathcal S^h(z)F_{21}^{-1}.
\]
Here \(|a|\) denotes the Cartan charge of a homogeneous state. The second formula uses the locality convention in which \(\mathcal S\) acts on the inputs of the product in the order \(a,b\). On a word of \(n\) states the field acquires the factor \(\exp(-\eta\sum_{i<j}B(|a_i|,|a_j|))\). For three charges \(a,b,c\), multiplying the first pair first gives the exponent \(-\eta(B(a,b)+B(a+b,c))\). Multiplying the last pair first gives \(-\eta(B(b,c)+B(a,b+c))\), the same sum of three pairings. This proves the assertion for any consecutive block by iteration. In an exchange the ratio of the two factors for the two orders gives the displayed conjugations. The original substitutions, exchange hexagon and Yang–Baxter identity therefore hold after twisting. The factors are constant in the positions, so all residues including their normal derivatives have the original pole bounds at each precision. [Rational affine field comparison](#ch12-theorem-rational-affine-field-comparison)

theorems.title: Proposition
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Proposition.** The coloured fields \(W=V_h^F\) have a factorizing ordered bar \(C(W)\). Its cut cobar \(A(W)\) has a coassociative, counital coproduct for the same-position tensor with middle passage \(y_b\otimes v_c\mapsto\chi(b,c)v_c\otimes y_b\). For the stated rank-three charges, the ordinary diagonal tensor admits no coproduct on this word object inducing \(\Delta^F\) at a singleton.

theorems.title: Torsion lengths in the exceptional universal \(W_4\) vacuum complex
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_4\), write \(\tau=k+4\). At
\[
\tau=\frac32,-\frac32,\frac23,-\frac23,
\]
the dimensions in degrees zero through fifteen are
\[
(1,0,0,1,0,1,0,1,2,1,1,1,2,0,0,1),
\]
and all higher groups vanish. The total dimension is twelve, whereas the generic exterior algebra on degrees \(3,5,7\) has dimension eight. The primitive products satisfy
\[
\eta_3\eta_5\ne0,\qquad
\eta_3\eta_7\ne0,\qquad
\eta_5\eta_7=0.
\]
Exactly two local torsion pairs, in degrees \((8,9)\) and \((11,12)\), account for the excess. To see what specialization detects, consider a two-term summand \(R\xrightarrow{\,t^\ell\,}R\) over a local parameter ring, with \(\ell\ge1\). Its differential is invertible after \(t\) is inverted and zero after \(t=0\). All positive \(\ell\) give the same two special-fibre dimensions. Lifting the lower generator, applying the differential, dividing by \(t\) and reducing again gives a nonzero map precisely for \(\ell=1\). This is the first Bockstein on that summand. In the local parameter \(t=\tau-\tau_0\), write the finite zero-weight differential as \(A+tB+O(t^2)\). On a class killed by \(A\), reduction of \(B\) modulo the image of \(A\) is the first Bockstein. In each of the two degrees its rank is one at both \(\tau_0=3/2\) and \(-3/2\). Indeed null vectors on opposite sides of the constant matrix have nonzero pairing through \(B\), detected modulo \(1000003\) on maximal-rank minors. A single nonunit elementary divisor occurs in each degree, so it has valuation one. The reciprocal parameter change takes a uniformizer to a unit times a uniformizer. Thus both torsion summands are \(R/(t)\) at each of the four points, for \(R=\mathbb C[\tau]_{(\tau-\tau_0)}\). [CQ8](#ref-ch12-cq8), [CQ12](#ref-ch12-cq12)
