theorems.title: Theorem (formality of the exceptional \(W_4\) vacuum)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (formality of the exceptional \(W_4\) vacuum).** For the universal principal \(\mathfrak{sl}_4\) vacuum in all smooth weak modules at \(\tau_0=-3/2\), the quartic coefficient \(\gamma\) vanishes. Its derived endomorphism algebra is formal as an associative dg algebra. The reciprocal equivalence and complementary duality give the same formality at \(\tau_0=3/2,\,2/3,\,-2/3\).

theorems.title: Counterexample (two unimodular lattices)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Counterexample (two unimodular lattices).** Let \(L\) be a positive-definite even integral lattice. Its underlying abelian group is free of finite rank, its symmetric pairing is integral, and every squared length \((\alpha,\alpha)\) is even. The lattice vertex algebra \(V_L\) has a Heisenberg Fock space for each charge \(\alpha\in L\). Its irreducible ordinary modules are indexed by \(L^*/L\), where
\[
L^*=\{x\in L\otimes\mathbb R:(x,L)\subset\mathbb Z\}.
\]
For a unimodular lattice \(L^*=L\), so the vacuum is the only simple ordinary module. Every object in the finite semisimple category is a sum of copies of that unit. Fusion, exchange and twist then give the ribbon category of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces with its ordinary flip and identity twist.

Take \(L=E_8\oplus E_8\) and \(L=D_{16}^{+}\). Both give this category, central charge sixteen and the same torus character. In both theories weight one has dimension \(496\). The two nondegenerate complex pairings are isometric, so even the double-pole test can agree under an identification of the state spaces. Now take the simple-pole test on *all* pairs of weight-one states. It gives respectively
\[
\mathfrak e_8\oplus\mathfrak e_8
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathfrak{so}_{32}.
\]
In the first algebra two nonzero commuting simple ideals exhaust the space. The second algebra is simple. An isomorphism preserving all the residues would transport the first decomposition to such a decomposition of the second. Thus the ribbon category, central charge, torus character and isometry class of the pairing together admit no reconstruction inverse on these two algebras. [Dong–Mason, Theorem 2, Lemma 2.1 and the proof at \(c=16\)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0203005#page=2) · [GR1](#ref-ch13-gr1)

theorems.title: Theorem (ordinary classical reconstruction)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (ordinary classical reconstruction).** Fix an ordinary unital Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral algebra \(A\) on a smooth separated complex algebraic curve \(X\). For arbitrary classical parameter schemes \(T\to X^I\), its complete ordinary coefficient-family categories form a quasi-coherent-linear unital weak factorization system. They have categorical base change, coherent collision equivalences for every surjection, unit insertions, separated external fusion, and compatible evaluation on the minimal coefficient. The empty category is \(\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb C}\), and its inserted vacuum realizes \(\operatorname{Fact}(A)\), including the normalized empty algebra and all collision extensions. Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Rec}\bigl(\mathcal C(A),F\bigr)\cong A.
\]
All tensors are ordinary. Category tensors are taken among locally presentable complex-linear categories and cocontinuous functors; descent is Zariski. No flatness or finite-generation condition is imposed on action coefficient modules, and parameter schemes may be nonreduced or have coincident marked sections. [GR1, Theorem 9.1](#ref-ch13-gr1)

theorems.title: Lemma (base change for the action kernel)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Lemma (base change for the action kernel).** For every homomorphism \(B\to B'\), the canonical comparison
\[
B'\otimes_B\ker\mu_M
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\ker(B'\otimes_B\mu_M)
\]
is an isomorphism.

theorems.title: Example (derived restriction at a point)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (derived restriction at a point).** For the closed point \(t=0\) on the affine line, a free resolution of its residue field is multiplication by \(t\) between two copies of \(\mathbb C[t]\). Tensor it with the left differential module
\[
\delta_0=\mathbb C[s],\qquad
t=-\frac d{ds},\qquad\partial_t=s.
\]
Multiplication by \(t\) is surjective with one-dimensional kernel. Hence
\[
\mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb C[t]}\delta_0=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Tor}_1^{\mathbb C[t]}(\mathbb C,\delta_0)=\mathbb C.
\]
Ordinary and derived restriction differ even on this elementary coefficient. The theorem concerns a fixed \(A\) and classical parameters; it does not establish a derived or physical reconstruction, or a theorem for an arbitrary nonflat family in which \(A\) itself varies.

theorems.title: Theorem (supported Vandermonde pro-duality)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (supported Vandermonde pro-duality).** For one Heisenberg current on the affine line with a chosen coordinate, use the Cousin differential with zero central contractions. For every finite position set \(I\) and every number \(n\) of polar factors,
\[
\Phi_{I,n}=V_n^\sharp:
(\mathcal C^+_{I,n})^\sharp
\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal C^-_{I,n})^\sharp
\]
is an isomorphism of the full supported pro-diagrams and their dual vacuum triangles. It retains all finite normal derivatives and the spectator extension at three positions, and commutes with finite-stage numerical specialization of \(\kappa\). Its cut products are intertwined by the cross Vandermonde factors. [GR4](#ref-ch13-gr4)

theorems.title: Open problem (the forward exterior contact)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Open problem (the forward exterior contact).** At two positions write \(U\to V\to W\xrightarrow{\epsilon}U[1]\) for the reversed exterior pro-dual triangle above. Can one construct a triangle \(G'\to G\to G''\xrightarrow{g}G'[1]\) for the original regular exterior contact, together with continuous endpoint maps \(f:U\to G'\) and \(h:W\to G''\) such that \(f[1]\epsilon\simeq gh\)? The homotopy must respect the transitions on composite states, both vacuum maps, the original scalar contact and the cuts. At three positions it must retain the collision of positions 1 and 3 with position 2 separate. [The reversed comparison](#ch13-theorem-supported-vandermonde-pro-duality) · [The forward comparison and its hypotheses](#ref-ch13-gr5)

theorems.title: Theorem (degree-zero mode algebra)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (degree-zero mode algebra).** For the stated rational exchange and direct-sum totalization, placing the labelled inputs in their standard order induces
\[
 \mathsf M_U(V)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^0(G_U(V)).
\]

theorems.title: The weak Hopf algebra of Ising sectors
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For the Ising model \((p,q)=(3,4)\), the simples \(1,\psi,\sigma\) satisfy
\[
\psi^2=1,\qquad\psi\sigma=\sigma,\qquad
\sigma^2=1+\psi.
\]
A faithful additive tensor functor to finite vector spaces with scalar unit would give positive integer dimensions with
\[
d_\psi^2=1,\qquad d_\sigma^2=1+d_\psi=2,
\]
which is impossible. The finite-base functor has no such problem. Its \(\sigma\)-bimodule has the following dimensions, in row and column order \(1,\psi,\sigma\)
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&1\\
0&0&1\\
1&1&0
\end{pmatrix},
\]
so the ordinary vector dimensions of \(F(1),F(\psi),F(\sigma)\) are \(3,3,4\). Consequently
\[
H\cong\operatorname{Mat}_3(\mathbb C)
\oplus\operatorname{Mat}_3(\mathbb C)
\oplus\operatorname{Mat}_4(\mathbb C),
\qquad\dim H=34.
\]
In \(V_\sigma\otimes V_\sigma\) there are sixteen pairs of basis vectors. Fix the intermediate sector. If it is \(1\) there is one matching pair, and if it is \(\psi\) there is one. At \(\sigma\) there are two choices at each outer end, hence four pairs. Thus \(\Delta(1)\) has rank \(1+1+4=6\), the dimension of \(F(1)\oplus F(\psi)\) required by \(\sigma^2=1+\psi\).

theorems.title: Example (two affine vacua)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (two affine vacua).** Put a copy of \(L(0)\) at each of \(0,1\), with vacuum tensor \(v=|0\rangle\otimes|0\rangle\). Take a Cartan element \(H\) with \((H,H)\ne0\) and the functions \(f(w)=w\) and \(g(w)=1/w+2/(w-1)\). Write \(H_n^{(s)}\) for the mode \(H\otimes(w-s)^n\) on the factor at \(s\). All \(H_n^{(s)}\) with \(n\ge0\) kill \(v\), so
\[
(H\otimes f)v=0,\qquad
(H\otimes g)v=(H_{-1}^{(0)}+2H_{-1}^{(1)})v.
\]
The linear coefficient of \(f\) at each point is \(1\). Since \([H_1,H_{-1}]=(H,H)K\) at either point, the commutator of these two currents sends \(v\) to \(3k(H,H)v\). The residues of \(g\,df\) at \(0\) and \(1\) are \(1\) and \(2\). In the geometric local coordinate \(u=1/w\) at infinity, \(g=3u+O(u^2)\) and \(g\,df=(-3u^{-1}+O(1))\,du\). Reading powers of \(u\) as output mode indices would pair \(H_{-1}\) with \(3H_1\), giving the opposite central scalar. Equivariance would then force even the vacuum intertwiner, which sends \(v\) to \(|0\rangle\), to vanish.

theorems.title: Theorem (derived fusion of integrable modules)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (derived fusion of integrable modules).** At the stated positive integral level and distinct points \(p,q\), the higher fusion functors on simple integrable inputs satisfy
\[
L_b\odot\bigl(L(\lambda),L(\mu)\bigr)
\cong
\bigoplus_{\nu\in P_k^+}
N_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}L(\nu)
\otimes H_b(\Omega G;\mathbb C).
\]
The formula extends additively to finite sums of these inputs. The integers \(N_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\) are the Verlinde fusion multiplicities. The index \(b\) is homological; in the cohomological convention it contributes in degree \(-b\). [GR8](#ref-ch13-gr8)

theorems.title: Example (Two first jets on an M2 line)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
For \(n\ge2\) let \(E=E_{12}\) send the second basis vector to the first. Write \(J(H)\) for the universal line generator labelled by the matrix-valued polynomial \(H\). Apply the two first-jet operations \(J(Ez)\) and \(J(Ew)\) in opposite time orders and subtract. At tree level their bracket is the matrix commutator with Moyal multiplication of the entries. Both orders contain the matrix factor \(E^2=0\). At one loop the bulk operator product has a second colour contraction. For labels \(E_{ij}z,E_{kl}w\) it leaves the product of the two constant generators \(J(E_{il})J(E_{kj})\). Every other term in the one-loop formula is multiplied by \(\delta_{jk}\) or \(\delta_{il}\). On the chosen pair both deltas vanish, so in the order and normalisation of Costello's (9.3.11) the bulk dual gives
\[
 [J(Ez),J(Ew)]
   =\frac{h_{\mathrm b}}{32\pi^2}\,J(E)^2+O(h_{\mathrm b}^2).
\]
The constant algebra embeds in the classical enveloping algebra by the Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem. In this subalgebra \(U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)\), \(E\) acts on two copies of the defining representation by \(E\otimes1+1\otimes E\). Its square sends \(e_2\otimes e_2\) to \(2e_1\otimes e_1\). Replacing this product by multiplication of the colour matrices would discard a nonzero output. [Costello, §9.3, equation (9.3.11)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.02500#page=42)

The brane description begins with two matrices \(B_1,B_2\) acting on \(\mathbb C^K\) and maps \(I:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^K\), \(P:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^n\). The classical equation is \([B_1,B_2]+IP=c\,1_K\), modulo changes of basis in \(\mathbb C^K\). Quantum Hamiltonian reduction gives its protected operator algebra. The generators labelled by transverse monomials come from the framed words \(PB_1^rB_2^sI\) with their colour indices contracted against a matrix. In the presentation valid uniformly in \(K\), interchanging the two first-jet words can join their colour indices or contract their transverse letters. The two colour joins again require \(2=1\). The transverse contraction leaves two constant words, giving \(h_{\mathrm l}J(E)^2\) to first order in the brane parameter \(h_{\mathrm l}\).

At \(K=1\) this contraction is visible in the reduction itself. Write \(D,X\) for the conjugate centre-of-mass operators in the order \([D,X]=h_{\mathrm l}\). They commute with the constant off-diagonal flavour operator \(T\). The corresponding one-letter insertions give
\[
 [TD,TX]=T^2[D,X]=h_{\mathrm l}T^2 .
\]
For a finite numerical example take \(n=2\) and \(c/h_{\mathrm l}=4\). In the ordered reduction the moment equation on the framing variables \(r_1,r_2\) reads \(r_1\partial_{r_1}+r_2\partial_{r_2}+2=c/h_{\mathrm l}\). Thus homogeneous quadratics furnish a flavour module. With \(T=r_1\partial_{r_2}\), the commutator sends \(r_2^2\) to \(2h_{\mathrm l}r_1^2\).

On the uniform algebra, comparing the two first-order coefficients fixes \(h_{\mathrm l}=h_{\mathrm b}/(32\pi^2)\) to first order in these conventions. The reading is an operator coefficient, before choosing a state on the line. [Costello, §§1.5–1.7, Lemma 11.0.1 and §§13.1–13.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.02500#page=56)

theorems.title: Example (a relation between paths)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (a relation between paths).** Take the quiver
\[
1\mathrel{\mathop{\longrightarrow}^{a}}2
\mathrel{\mathop{\longrightarrow}^{b}}1
\]
over \(\mathbb C\), impose \(ab=0\), and multiply paths in the order they are traversed. Its path algebra \(R\) has basis
\[
e_1,e_2,a,b,ba.
\]
Let \(A=R/(Re_2R)\cong\mathbb C\), supported at vertex 1. The right projective modules have bases
\[
e_1R=\langle e_1,a\rangle,
\qquad e_2R=\langle e_2,b,ba\rangle.
\]
A projective resolution of \(A\) is
\[
0\longrightarrow e_1R
\xrightarrow{\,b\cdot\,}e_2R
\xrightarrow{\,a\cdot\,}e_1R
\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow0.
\]
Indeed, the first map sends \(e_1,a\) to \(b,ba\), so it is injective. The second sends \(e_2\) to \(a\) and kills \(b,ba\). Its image is precisely the kernel of \(e_1R\to A\). The composite is zero because \(ab=0\).

theorems.title: Theorem: the flux class in derived particle composition
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem: the flux class in derived particle composition.** For every integer \(N\ge1\) and every numerical \(\hbar\ne0\), \(\phi_N\) is surjective. Its kernel \(I_N\) is generated by the Newton relation \(e_{N+1}\), the elementary symmetric polynomial expressed in the power sums \(J(x^k)\), and \(I_N^2=I_N\). Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_1(A_N,A_N)=0.
\]
To identify a degree-two contribution, quotient the Weyl Lie algebra by its scalar centre. Two lifts of elements of this quotient can have a scalar commutator even when their classes commute; for instance \([x,y]=\hbar 1\). This scalar defect defines the class of the central extension
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathbb C1\longrightarrow\mathfrak g
\longrightarrow\mathfrak g/\mathbb C1\longrightarrow0
\]
and will be denoted by \(\omega\). Capping a degree-two sewing class with \(\omega\) evaluates it on that extension and gives a split surjection of \(A_N\)-bimodules
\[
\omega\mathbin{\frown}-:
\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\twoheadrightarrow A_N.
\]
Every sewing Tor group is a possibly infinite direct sum of the bimodules
\[
D(\tau)=(\tau\otimes W_\hbar^{\otimes N})^{S_N},
\]
where \(\tau\) runs through irreducible representations of \(S_N\). These modules are projective separately on the left and on the right. The cap kernel is canonically \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U(\mathfrak g)}_2(A_N,A_N)\), while its splitting requires a choice. At \(N=1\), the cap is an isomorphism; for \(N\ge2\), the kernel's multiplicities remain to be determined. See [*The junction with its flux class*, Theorems 4–6](#ref-ch14-01).

theorems.title: A vanishing flux square and its locality obstruction
theorems.statement_excerpt:
What happens if one inserts the flux twice? Write \(\mathfrak l=\mathfrak g/\mathbb C1\), and lift each polynomial Weyl symbol to its representative with zero constant term. The constant part of the commutator of two lifts is a scalar two-cocycle \(\omega\) on \(\mathfrak l\). Its class acts on the two-sided interval by cap product. Its square vanishes in algebraic cohomology at every numerical \(\hbar\ne0\), even though its four-input representative is nonzero. For example,
\[
 (\omega\wedge\omega)(x,y,x^3,y^3)=3\hbar^4 .
\]
In the Moyal formula the constant coefficient of \([x^d,y^d]\) for odd \(d\) is \(c_d=2d!(\hbar/2)^d\); mixed degrees contribute no constant. The displayed value is \(2c_1c_3\).

Vanishing of the square means finding a three-cochain \(H\) whose differential is the displayed four-cochain on every input. Such a primitive comes from cyclic homology of the polynomial Weyl algebra. The normalized Hochschild chain \(u=\hbar^{-1}x[y]\) has \(bu=1\). Its Connes boundary \(Bu=\hbar^{-1}(1[x|y]-1[y|x])\) generates top Hochschild homology and survives in cyclic degree two. Thus the unit gives a nonzero ordinary cyclic degree-two class. Choose an algebraic cyclic two-cocycle \(\Phi\) on unnormalized chains with \(\Phi(1,1,1)=1\). Antisymmetrizing \(\Phi\) gives a closed Lie three-cochain on \(\mathfrak g\). For the chosen lift \(s:\mathfrak l\to\mathfrak g\), let \(P\) be its restriction to the three lifted inputs and put \(\beta(a)=\Phi(1,1,sa)\). The cyclic cocycle identity gives \(dP=\omega\wedge(\omega-d\beta)\). Hence \(H=P+\omega\wedge\beta\) satisfies \(dH=\omega\wedge\omega\). Contraction by \(H\) gives a bimodule homotopy for the two successive cap operations. At rank one, where the cap in degree two is an isomorphism, the component of the *outgoing cut* from degree four to two degree-two factors is zero. The higher Tor groups themselves are not determined by this identity.

What transverse data would a field theory need to produce this homotopy? The Taylor jet of order \(L\) at the origin keeps the coefficients of monomials of total degree at most \(L\). Choose distinct odd \(d,e>L\). All four inputs \(x^d,y^d,x^e,y^e\) have zero \(L\)-jet. In each term of the differential of a three-cochain, two of those inputs remain untouched after bracketing the other two. A three-cochain depending only on \(L\)-jets therefore has zero differential on this tuple. Yet \(\omega\wedge\omega\) takes the value \(2c_dc_e\ne0\). This works for every finite \(L\). The algebraic primitive admits arbitrarily high jets of polynomial inputs. To realize it on a physical interval one must specify the endpoint actions and a contact homotopy in the allowed space of distributions, and recover both the cap and the outgoing cut with the chosen regularization.

theorems.title: Theorem: integral curved comparison
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem: integral curved comparison.** For \(1\le N\le3\), there is a strictly unital \(R\)-linear \(A_\infty\) quasi-isomorphism
\[
K_N^{\mathrm{full}}\simeq_{A_\infty}e\Omega_S(C,w)e,
\]
without inverting or completing in \(\hbar\). Its derived zero fibre is formal, with algebra
\[
\left(\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_N,y_1,\ldots,y_N]
\otimes\Lambda(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_N)\right)^{S_N},
\qquad |\theta_i|=-1.
\]
The comparison uses ordered symbols and homotopy transfer over the polynomial parameter ring; the group-relative relations retain the permutation terms that ordinary symmetrization would lose. See [*The integral relative curved model*, main theorem](#ref-ch14-02).

theorems.title: Theorem (Hamiltonian transport through total degree 24)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (Hamiltonian transport through total degree 24).** Use the universal homology basis of ordered monomials in \(J(m)\) and \(z(m)=\operatorname{Tr}((\operatorname{Sym}m)\Psi)\), with \(m\) nonconstant and each odd generator \(z(m)\) used at most once. For the lower maps above, start with the homogeneous, alternating, \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-equivariant extension through arity five of Theorem 12.6. Its higher components vanish if an input is constant or quadratic. Keeping \(\Phi_1,\ldots,\Phi_4\) fixed, one can change \(\Phi_5\) by a closed cochain supported on five-tuples of total polynomial degrees \(22\) and \(23\). The resulting homotopy Lie map extends in every arity on tuples of total degree \(D\le24\), including tuples with linear inputs. Here \(D\) is the sum of the degrees in \(x,y\) on homogeneous inputs. With weights \(\deg(x,y,h,\nu)=(1,1,2,0)\), the physical weight shift of \(\Phi_n\) is \(2-2n\). The construction is polynomial over \(\mathbb Q[\nu,h]\) and specializes to every positive rank over \(\mathbb Q[h]\). [*Polynomial Hamiltonian transport*, Theorem 14.2](#ref-ch14-05)

theorems.title: Conditional theorem (universal arity five with a fixed ternary map)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Conditional theorem (universal arity five with a fixed ternary map).** Assume the universal Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt homology model with cycle lifts, injectivity after specialization at sufficiently large positive ranks in each fixed weight, and the ordered-symbol comparison for the effective trace complex. Assume also the all-weight calculation of \(H_3(\mathfrak q)\), in which no summand of highest weight \(m\le w-6\) occurs in weight \(w\). Then the specified \(\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3\), including the same \(Z_3\), extend through arity five on every polynomial input over \(\mathbb Q[\nu,h]\). A closed adjustment of \(\Phi_4\) is allowed. [*Universal arity-five obstruction*, §§5–8](#ref-ch14-05)

theorems.title: Theorem: the exact chiral image
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem: the exact chiral image.** For every \(N\ge1\), the framed relative complex has cohomology only in degree zero, in every conformal weight. Its algebra \(K_N\) is simple, with central charge \(-3N^2\) and a nondegenerate invariant form normalized on the vacuum. The natural map is injective and
\[
\alpha_N(K_N)=\ker(\chi^-_{(0)}:V_N\to V_N),
\qquad \chi^-=\phi\gamma.
\]
There is an odd global section \(\tau\) of conformal weight zero satisfying
\[
\chi^-_{(0)}\tau=N,
\qquad
V_N=\alpha_N(K_N)\oplus\tau_{(-1)}\alpha_N(K_N)
\]
as graded vector spaces. Thus the map is not surjective at any rank. The complementary factors are
\[
K_N=W_N\otimes\mathrm{Sb}\otimes\mathrm{SF},
\qquad
V_N=W_N\otimes\mathrm{Sb}\otimes bc.
\]
Here \(\mathrm{Sb}\) consists of the trace symplectic bosons and \(W_N\) is the common commuting factor. The two fermionic factors can be read in the same normalization: the \(bc\) pair has \(b=\chi^-/N\) of weight one and \(c=\tau\) of weight zero, with \(b_{(0)}c=1\). The symplectic-fermion algebra \(\mathrm{SF}\) is generated by \(b,\partial c\). The total unframed relative cohomology is \(K_N\) for \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) and \(W_N\) for \(\mathfrak{sl}_N\), with ghost number matching framing fermion number. For \(N\ge2\), the traceless quadratic currents generate affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at level \(-(N^2-1)/2\); their zero modes give the Lie action used below. See [*Global sections on the Hilbert scheme*, Theorems A–B](#ref-ch14-06).

theorems.title: Relation weights in rank-two chiral cohomology
theorems.statement_excerpt:
At fixed conformal weight \(H\), reduced fermion number \(f\) and flavour weight \(F\), every finite torsion interval \([i,j)\) in the reduced two-chart complex on \(\operatorname{Hilb}^2(\mathbb C^2)\) satisfies
\[
                 2j-|f|\ \ge\ |F|.
\]
In an irreducible multiplet of highest weight \(m\), the relation has torus weight \(j-f/2\ge m/2+\max(0,-f)\).

theorems.title: Generator weights at fixed horizontal spin
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Fix conformal weight \(H\) and reduced fermion number \(f\in\mathbb Z\) in the polynomial two-chart complex on \(\operatorname{Hilb}^2(\mathbb C^2)\). If its degree-one cohomology in torus weight \(\ell-f/2\) contains \(\operatorname{Sym}^m\mathbb C^2\) under the divided horizontal \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) action, then \(2\ell-|f|\ge -m-2\). Every finite interval \([i,j)\) in the multiplicity space of this representation satisfies
\[
 |f|-2i-2\ \le\ m\ \le\ 2j-|f|,\qquad i+j\ \ge\ |f|-1 .
\]
The degree and interval bounds hold after completion of each fixed sector. The first positive even-charge singlets attain equality in both interval bounds and in the degree bound at birth.

theorems.title: Torsion intervals at torus-finite specialization
theorems.statement_excerpt: Complete the direct sum of the reduced rank-two chart complexes \(\hbar\)-adically, take the torus-finite part of \(H^1\), then specialize at \(\hbar=1\). The torsion intervals contribute zero exactly when their torus birth weights have a uniform lower bound. Otherwise their contribution has complex dimension \(2^{\aleph_0}\).

theorems.title: Specialization at bounded horizontal spin
theorems.statement_excerpt: The finite torsion intervals of bounded horizontal highest weight contribute zero to torus-finite specialization. On the infinite support of any representative of a nonzero class in the torsion-interval contribution, the reduced births \(\mu\) tend to \(-\infty\), while the reduced charges \(f\), highest weights \(m\), relation weights \(\delta\) and lengths \(j-i\) tend to \(+\infty\). The same assertions hold with the global spectator factors adjoined before completion.

theorems.title: Torus-finite classes and separated completion in rank two
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let \(E\) be \(H^1\) of the formal chiral sheaf on \(\operatorname{Hilb}^2(\mathbb C^2)\) with its geometric two-chart transition, either reduced or with the global symplectic-boson and \(bc\) factors adjoined before completion. Write \(\widehat E_{\rm sep}=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}E/t^rE\), with \(t=\hbar\) of torus weight one. For a module \(M\) with this torus action, let \(M_{\rm fin}\) be its finite sums of weight vectors. The natural projection induces an isomorphism of graded \(\mathbb C[t]\)-modules
\[
 E_{\rm fin}\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ (\widehat E_{\rm sep})_{\rm fin}
\]
and an isomorphism of their specializations at \(t=1\).

theorems.title: The order of separated surface collars
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (the order of two surface collars).** Prepare one level-one current excitation on the second surface and the vacuum on the first. The part of the response odd under exchanging the two collars tests the derivative term of the Miura product. Put \(\tau=\hbar_{\mathrm b}/(4\pi^2)\). With the elementary right action \(Y=a\partial_X\), level-one unit surfaces, and incoming magnetic strength \(q_i=\tau/c_{\mathrm M}\) for Moyal parameter \([z,w]_* =c_{\mathrm M}\ne0\), the order-odd response to the test \(f(z)=z^2/2\) is \(\tau(j_2[f']-j_1[f'])/2\). Here \(j_i[f']=\operatorname{Res}f'(z)j^{(i)}(z)dz\). On \(|0\rangle_1\otimes j^{(2)}_{-1}|0\rangle_2\), the current in the second factor returns the vacuum and the first contributes zero. The reading is \(+\tau/2\) times the vacuum. Write \(S=J_1+J_2\) and \(Q=J_1J_2+\tfrac a2(\partial J_2-\partial J_1)\) for the first two elementary Weyl coefficients. The Miura stress tensor \(T=({:}S^2{:}-2Q)/(2k)\) gives the order-odd reading \(+a/2\) on the same marked vector at \(k=1\), fixing \(a=\tau\) at this order and in these markings. Integration by parts gives \(-a/2\) for the order-odd reading of \(Q\). At \(a=0,\ k=1\), the fourth pole of \(T(z)T(w)\) has vacuum coefficient one. An independently prepared magnetic flux must be compared with the stated incoming strength.

theorems.title: Theorem (endomorphisms of the co-vacuum)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (endomorphisms of the co-vacuum).** Assume \(\mathfrak g\) is finite-dimensional and two-step nilpotent,
\([\mathfrak g,[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g]]=0\).
Then its internally graded derived endomorphism algebra has a strict multiplicative model
\[
\operatorname{REnd}(W_n)\simeq
U(P_n)\ltimes\operatorname{Sym}(N_n^\vee[-1]),
\qquad d=0.
\]
The dual is restricted by internal weight; the symmetric algebra is graded-commutative. Its ghost generators have degree \(2-n\), so they are polynomial for \(n=2\) and exterior for \(n=3\). For \(p\in P_n\) and \(v\in N_n\), define \(\rho(p)v\) by taking the mixed bracket \([p,v]\), passing to its top cohomology class and choosing the unique representative in \(N_n\). Thus \(\rho\) is the projected principal-part action: multiply a Laurent principal part by the regular polynomial, discard terms in which a pole disappears, and include the bracket of the Lie-algebra coefficients. The mixed relation is
\[
[X_p,c_\lambda]=-c_{\lambda\circ\rho(p)}.
\]
The cancelled-pole example above therefore has zero projected coefficient. Starting with \([z_1^{-2}z_2^{-1}]\) instead gives the surviving class \([z_1^{-1}z_2^{-1}]\) with the Lie bracket of the two colours. This is the projection that enters the ghost commutator. All modes are retained, with algebraic sums and products. [*Higher current algebras and their induced modules*, Theorem 13.2](#ref-ch14-09).

theorems.title: Example (four distinct colours)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (four distinct colours).** Let \(E_{ij}\) be the matrix taking the \(j\)-th coordinate vector to the \(i\)-th and killing the others. Use the basis \(T_{ij}=E_{ij}-E_{ji}\), \(i<j\), orthonormal for \(K(X,Y)=-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_{8}(XY)\). The matrices \(T_{12},T_{34}\) commute. Only a generator sharing an index with each of them can contribute to the contracted tensor. Summing over \(T_{13},T_{14},T_{23},T_{24}\) gives, with \(J_{ij}=J_{T_{ij}}[0,0]\),
\[
\begin{gathered}
 C_{12,34}{}^{cd}:J_cJ_d:\\
 =-2\bigl(:J_{13}J_{24}:-:J_{14}J_{23}:\bigr).
\end{gathered}
\]
Denote the two products on the right by \(B,C\) in the order shown, and the direct product \(:J_{12}J_{34}:\) by \(A\). The Killing form used in the published formula is \(6\operatorname{tr}_8=-12K\). If all other propagator conventions are fixed, the parameter multiplying the inverse of our form is consequently \(\hbar_K=-\hbar_{\mathrm{CP}}/12\). Each pair on the right has disjoint indices. Its two currents have zero bracket, so exchanging their order introduces no derivative commutator. Thus the simple pole of the two commuting first jets has a component along \(B-C\). It takes values in the weight-two fields. A scalar vacuum expectation by itself would discard those output colours.

theorems.title: Example (an ordered product on the punctured plane)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (an ordered product on the punctured plane).** Take a normal slice to the line and remove its origin. For \(R=\mathbb C[x,y]\), the open charts \(D(x)=\{x\ne0\}\) and \(D(y)=\{y\ne0\}\) have rings \(R_x,R_y\). On the overlap both coordinates are invertible. The ordered Čech complex is \(R_x\oplus R_y\to R_{xy}\) in degrees zero and one, with differential \((a,b)\mapsto b-a\). On an overlap cochain \(w\), left multiplication by \((a,b)\) uses \(aw\) and right multiplication uses \(wb\). Its degree-zero classes are polynomials. Its degree-one classes are represented by linear combinations of \(x^{-i}y^{-j}\), \(i,j\ge1\). The cohomology products \(x[x^{-1}y^{-1}]\) and \([x^{-1}y^{-1}]y\) vanish, but they have different primitives. \(1/y\) extends over \(D(y)\), and \(1/x\) extends over \(D(x)\). Take the two primitives \((0,1/y)\) and \((-1/x,0)\). Multiply the first on the right by \(y\), and subtract the product of \(x\) with the second. The result is \((1,1)\). Changing either primitive changes this answer by an element of \((x,y)\). Thus the triple Massey product is \(1+(x,y)\), and contains no zero. The ordered differential algebra on the punctured plane retains a homotopy that cannot be read from its two cohomology products.

theorems.title: Conditional theorem (completed cut cobar)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Conditional theorem (completed cut cobar).** Suppose for every \(N\) the fully specified current source gives a connected coaugmented collision coalgebra \(C_N\), factorizing over each \(U_p\), compatible with derived change of coefficients. Then \(A_N=\Omega_{\rm cut}C_N\) is an associative chiral algebra for the consecutive-cut convolution. The connected bar–cobar mapping-space equivalence applies at each \(N\); taking the derived inverse limit gives the corresponding complete object. At each fixed arity only finitely many positive cut words occur, so the conclusion allows an infinite tower of transverse currents.

theorems.title: Corollary
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Corollary.** For \(N\ge2\), the product boundary condition gives a jointly faithful realization of the full algebraic level-zero chiral cotangent Yangian of \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) and its ordered local vertex coproduct in the marked field sector of this engineered theory. The scalar observation on a word can be taken on one enclosing tube. To cut the word, use a tube around each block.

theorems.title: Example (the two framing chambers)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (the two framing chambers).** On \(T^*\mathbb P^1\) the fixed points \(p_1,p_2\) are the coordinate lines. Give the two coordinates weights \(a_1,a_2\) and their cotangent partners weights \(\hbar-a_1,\hbar-a_2\). In this calculation \(u=a_1-a_2\) is the framing difference. The function called \(u\) on the affine cone was the matrix entry \(m_{12}\). A stable envelope extends a fixed-point class to equivariant cohomology with support in its attracting closure and diagonal value given by a signed Euler class. In the polarization with base tangent weights \((-u,u)\), these conditions and the off-diagonal degree bound determine the two chamber maps \(S_\pm\). Over \(\mathbb C(a_1,a_2,\hbar)\) both are invertible. Their change of basis, in fixed-point order \(p_1,p_2\), is
\[
 S_-^{-1}S_+=\frac{1}{u+\hbar}
 \begin{pmatrix}u&\hbar\\ \hbar&u\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For the one-vertex quiver with no arrows, the full carrier uses \(T^*\operatorname{Gr}(v,2)\) for \(v=0,1,2\). The extreme varieties are points. For a doublet with basis \(e_+,e_-\), put \(e_{ij}=e_i\otimes e_j\). Splitting the framing gives the ordered basis \(e_{++},e_{+-},e_{-+},e_{--}\) of the localized tensor square. The displayed block acts on the middle two vectors and the two extremes are fixed. Hence \(R(u)=(uI+\hbar P)/(u+\hbar)\), where \(P\) interchanges the doublets. The formula is regular for \(u+\hbar\ne0\). For \(\hbar\ne0\) the antisymmetric-to-symmetric eigenvalue ratio is \((u-\hbar)/(u+\hbar)\).

theorems.title: The one-loop cobar on finite root jets
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (the one-loop cobar on finite root jets).** The augmented algebra map
\[
 F_R:\Omega(W)\longrightarrow S_R,\qquad
 x(J_i)\longmapsto i!\,a_i,\qquad
 x(w)\longmapsto0\quad\text{if \(w\) has charge greater than one}
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism in every charge over \(R\). The derivative at the origin is \(i!\) times the coefficient of \(x^i\). For an input monomial of total root degree \(d\ge2\), the two terms \(f+sf\) and \(\hbar(f-sf)/u\) both vanish at the origin because their degrees are \(d\) and \(d-1\) whenever they are nonzero. Thus only the constant and the two linear inputs contribute to \(\bar\Delta J_0^2\). Their evaluations give \(2J_0\otimes J_0+\hbar(J_1\otimes J_0-J_0\otimes J_1)\). Substituting \(x(J_0)\mapsto a_0\) and \(x(J_1)\mapsto a_1\) in the cobar differential gives \(2a_0^2+\hbar(a_1a_0-a_0a_1)\) before imposing the target relations. This is the coefficient of \(z^1w^0\) in the difference of the two sides of the exchange relation, so it vanishes in \(S_R\). The scalar unit maps to the scalar unit.

theorems.title: Example (The order of two simple factors on K3)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Take \(i\ne j\) and a nonzero class \(\xi\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_i,L_j)\). Its extension has the form
\[
 0\longrightarrow L_j\longrightarrow M_\xi
   \longrightarrow L_i\longrightarrow0 .
\]
Can the same middle object be formed in the opposite order? Applying \(\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,-)\) shows what a reversed flag would require. The connecting map sends the identity of \(L_i\) to \(\xi\), so no nonzero scalar multiple of the identity lifts. Since \(\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,L_j)=0\), this gives \(\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M_\xi)=0\). Applying \(\operatorname{Hom}(L_j,-)\) instead gives \(\operatorname{Hom}(L_j,M_\xi)=\mathbb C\), spanned by the inclusion. Every nonzero multiple has the same image. With \(e_i=1_{[L_i]}\) and the quotient-first convention (15.1), the two fibres are a point and the empty set. Hence
\[
 (e_i*e_j)(M_\xi)=1,\qquad (e_j*e_i)(M_\xi)=0 .
\]
On \(L_i\oplus L_j\) both products take the value one. There is a further distinction even among the nonsplit objects. Changing bases at the two simple ends multiplies \(\xi\) by a nonzero scalar. Any isomorphism between two such middle objects must preserve their unique subobject of type \(L_j\), so their isomorphism classes are parametrised by \(\mathbb P\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_i,L_j)\simeq\mathbb P^1\). A flag in \(M_\xi\) with simple successive quotients has length two and these two factors. All the other words in simple indicators vanish on this family. Thus every function in the ordinary algebra generated by the three simple indicators is constant on this projective line of nonisomorphic sheaves.

theorems.title: Theorem (ordinary K3 Hall comparison)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (ordinary K3 Hall comparison).** Choose the simultaneous cyclic minimal \(A_\infty\) model of the collection and a comparison with its Dolbeault category strictly unital over the quiver vertex-idempotent algebra \(\mathbb C^3\). There is a unique unital, charge-graded isomorphism
\[
\Theta:\mathcal C_\Pi\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_L
\]
sending the simple indicator at vertex \(i\) to \(1_{[L_i]}\). At every finite nilpotence bound it comes from an algebraic tensor family. Over reduced bases this family identifies reduced relative flag varieties, their subquotients, and all forgetting and regrouping maps. [Primitive recognition, Proposition “Regular families and the ordinary composition algebra”][ordinary-hall]

theorems.title: Lemma (lifting a principal part)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Lemma (lifting a principal part).** A map \(M_p\to H^0(C)=T\) with \(1\mapsto m\in\ker u^p\) lifts to a derived \(R'[D]\)-linear map \(M_p\to C\) exactly when \(u^{p-1}m=0\).

theorems.title: Proposition (the section cubic)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (the section cubic).** For \((\beta,d,m)=(C,1,0)\), identify \(S^{[1]}=S\). The complete coefficient is
\[
\mu(a,b)=\eta_1(a,C)\eta_1(b,C)C
\quad\text{on all }H^*(S,\mathbb Q).
\tag{15.8}
\]
The primary relative correspondence identifies this coefficient with the reduced genus-zero invariant of \(S\) in class \(C\). Each divisor insertion contributes its intersection with \(C\). The section meets \(F\) once, and the section invariant gives \(\eta_1(\mu(F,F),F)=1\), fixing the scalar multiplying the cubic. The other possible degree pattern \((0,2,4)\) vanishes by cyclicity and the unit identity. In particular
\[
\mu(C,C)=4C,\qquad \mu(C,F)=-2C,\qquad \mu(F,F)=C.
\]
This determines the product on all twenty-four states. Here \(F^{[1]}=F\) and the fibre-marked cap scalar is zero, so the fibre-marked tube reads precisely \(\mu(F,-)\). [Relative Donaldson–Thomas operators, the section cubic][section-cubic]

theorems.title: Example (Two sewings with one reduced section)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let \(p\in H^4(S,\mathbb Q)\) be the point class with \(\int_Sp=1\), and write \(a*b=a\cup b+\epsilon\mu(a,b)\) with \(\epsilon^2=0\). Use the three incoming states \(F,F,C\) and leave the outgoing state free. The ordinary products \(F\cup F=0\), \(F\cup C=p\) and \(C\cup C=-2p\), together with (15.8), give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (F*F)*C&=(\epsilon C)*C=-2\epsilon p,\\
 F*(F*C)&=F*(p-2\epsilon C)=-2\epsilon p .
\end{aligned}
\]
In the first sewing the reduced factor lies on the component carrying the two fibres. In the second, \(F\cup p=0\) by degree and \(\mu(F,p)=0\) by (15.8), so only the reduced product of \(F\) with \(C\) contributes. Opposite cuts give the same outgoing class. Pairing it with the ordinary unit gives the number \(-2\epsilon\). This checks the one-reduced-factor sewing rule on a specified compact curve class and specified boundary states. [The relative section coefficient and its geometric origin][section-cubic]

theorems.title: Scalar measurements recovering a compact first-order product
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Fix the rational cup algebra with its grading, unit and pairing. Keep all cap scalars, the full operator \(\mu(F,-)\), and every trace \(\operatorname{Tr}\mu(D,-)\). To measure the ambiguity of these data, subtract two commutative cyclic first-order corrections. Their difference \(\nu\) has degree \(-2\). A paired coefficient involving the unit vanishes, and the only remaining degree pattern consists of three degree-two states. The difference is therefore determined by the symmetric cubic \(T(a,b,c)=q(\nu(a,b),c)\) on \(V\).

Conversely, raise the third index of a symmetric cubic with \(q^{-1}\). Its first-order associator on middle classes is \((T(a,b,c)-T(b,c,a))p=0\). What does each of the two measurements impose? The marked row sets \(T(F,-,-)=0\). The trace of \(b\mapsto\nu(a,b)\) is \((\tau_qT)(a)=\sum_{ij}q^{ij}T(a,e_i,e_j)\) in any basis, so it sets \(\tau_qT=0\). The remaining cubics form
\[
 \ker\!\left(\operatorname{Sym}^3 L\xrightarrow{\ \tau_q\ }L\right),
 \qquad L=\operatorname{Ann}(F)\subset V^* .
\]
Here \(L\) has dimension \(21\), and \(q^{-1}|_L\) has rank \(20\). Contraction is onto. For example, choose \(\ell\in L\) with nonzero square. Contracting \(\ell^3\) yields a nonzero multiple of \(\ell\), and contracting \(\operatorname{sym}(\ell^2m)\) for \(m\perp\ell\) yields a nonzero multiple of \(m\). The dimension is \(\binom{23}{3}-21=1750\). These directions remain distinct even allowing a change of first-order splitting. A degree-minus-two Hochschild coboundary with the stated normalization has paired cubic \(\lambda(a)q(b,c)+\lambda(b)q(a,c)+\lambda(c)q(a,b)\). Its contraction is \(24\lambda\), so a trace-free coboundary of this form vanishes.

There is an explicit set of \(1750\) scalar insertions that recovers the missing coefficients. Subtract the known section reading from each measured cubic value to obtain \(T\). Put \(G=C+F\), so \(G^2=F^2=0\), \(q(F,G)=1\). Set \(W=\langle F,G\rangle^\perp\). For \(z\in W\) the state \(v(z)=G+z-q(z,z)F/2\) has square zero. Since \(T(F,-,-)=0\), its diagonal reading equals \(H(z)=T(G+z,G+z,G+z)\), a polynomial of degree at most three. The two terms of the inverse metric pairing \(F\) with \(G\) also drop out of the contraction. Thus trace-freeness becomes \(\Delta_WH=0\), with \(\Delta_W=\sum q_W^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j\). Choose \(s\in W\) of square \(a=2\), and write \(z=y+xs\) with \(y\in s^\perp\cap W\), a space of dimension \(19\). If \(\Delta'\) denotes its inverse-metric operator, the harmonic equation gives
\[
 H(y+xs)=A(y)+xB(y)-\tfrac a2x^2\Delta'A(y)
                         -\tfrac a6x^3\Delta'B(y)
\]
Here \(A,B\) are polynomials of degrees at most three and two. The formula determines all higher powers of \(x\) from \(A,B\) by the harmonic equation. To recover \(A\), set \(x=0\) and use the \(1540\) nonnegative integer tuples \(y\) of coordinate sum at most three in rational coordinates. The products \(\prod_i\binom{y_i}{j_i}\) with \(\sum_i j_i\le3\) have a triangular evaluation matrix on these tuples with diagonal one. This is the interpolation being used.

At \(x=1\), subtract the known contribution of \(A\). The \(210\) tuples of sum at most two determine \(B-a\Delta'B/6\). Applying \(1+a\Delta'/6\) recovers \(B\), since \((\Delta')^2B=0\). Homogenization and polarization then recover \(T\). Fewer than \(1750\) fixed scalar linear readings cannot separate a vector space of dimension \(1750\). These insertions solve the first-order algebraic inverse problem. A compact physical theory must still provide their preparation.

theorems.title: Pairwise recovery of a complex isotropic cubic
theorems.statement_excerpt: Let \(E=\langle C,F\rangle^\perp\) over \(\mathbb C\), with its nondegenerate symmetric intersection form \(q\) and \(\dim E=20\). For each prepared \(p\in E\), read the coefficient \(\lambda q(p,u)^3\) of \(t\) in the change from the section product on three copies of \(p\). To identify every nonzero tensor \(\lambda u^{\otimes3}\) with \(q(u,u)=0\), the minimum number of fixed probes is \(38\). Every list of at most \(37\) linear probes misses a pair of distinct tensors. A Zariski-open dense set of lists of \(38\) isotropic probe directions suffices.

theorems.title: The Weierstrass determinant on smooth genus-two curves
theorems.statement_excerpt:
There is a finite-dimensional geometric operator that produces the Igusa form itself. For a smooth complex genus-two curve \(C_2\), let \(W_6\) be its six Weierstrass points and \(H=H^0(C_2,\omega)\). Evaluate the fifth powers of holomorphic differentials:
\[
 e_5:\operatorname{Sym}^5 H\longrightarrow
            \bigoplus_{P\in W_6}\omega_P^{\,5}.
\]
Both sides have dimension six. In the coordinates \(y^2=a_6\prod_{i=1}^6(x-x_i)\), with \(\alpha=dx/y\) and \(\beta=x\,dx/y\), the evaluation matrix in the monomial basis has rows proportional to \((1,x_i,\ldots,x_i^5)\). The Wronskian fixes the proportionality in the determinant line. With \(\lambda=\det H\) the result is
\[
 d_e=a_6^5\!\prod_{i<j}(x_j-x_i)(\alpha\wedge\beta)^5
               \otimes\operatorname{or}(W_6)
       \ \in\lambda^5\otimes\operatorname{Or}(W_6).
\]
The final factor changes sign on an odd permutation of the six points. Write \(j\) for the Jacobian map from smooth genus-two curves to principally polarized abelian surfaces. In the period normalization of (15.10),
\[
 j^*\chi_{10}=\frac{d_e^2}{2^{32}\pi^{20}},\qquad
 j^*D_5=-\frac{d_e}{2^{16}\pi^{10}} .
\]
The unsquared sign uses the orientation fixed on the bielliptic family. To extend that calibration to all smooth curves, first compare the squares as algebraic sections. The determinant \(d_e\) is nowhere zero when the six roots are distinct. A smooth genus-two Jacobian has an irreducible theta divisor, the Abel image of the curve. It therefore avoids the decomposable locus on which \(\chi_{10}\) vanishes. The weight-ten modular form is an algebraic section of the tenth Hodge power, and its pullback by the Jacobian map is algebraic. Hence \(d_e^2/j^*\chi_{10}\) is an invertible regular function on the smooth locus. The period normalization can change this comparison by a nonzero constant.

Pull the ratio back to binary sextics with nonzero discriminant. The units in the polynomial ring of coefficients localized at the irreducible discriminant are \(c\,\operatorname{Disc}^k\). Multiplying the sextic by a nonzero complex scalar gives an isomorphic curve and multiplies its discriminant by the tenth power of that scalar. The ratio is intrinsic to the curve, so \(k=0\). The calibrated equality of squares now holds throughout the smooth locus. With the orientation lines identified, the ratio of the unsquared sections has fixed square on the connected smooth moduli space. Its value on the bielliptic family fixes the sign everywhere in that frame.

For the ordered roots \(0,1,2,4,7,11\) in a monic sextic the fifteen factors multiply to \(838252800\). Thus the coefficient of \((\alpha\wedge\beta)^{10}\) in \(j^*\chi_{10}\) is \(10721859080625/(65536\pi^{20})\). This constructs a section on smooth curves. Preparing the evaluation by a compact \(S\times E\) operation and extending that operation to stable degenerations remain separate problems.

theorems.title: Example (Composing two scale tests)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Choose a nonnegative even smooth function \(b\) supported in \((-\eta,\eta)\), with \(\int b^2\,du=1\) and \(0<\eta<\tfrac14\log(7/6)\). Let \(R_t b(u)=b(u-t)\). A pulse \(f_j=R_{\log j}b\) tests a scale close to \(j\). Substituting \(t=v+\log i\) in the convolution integral gives
\[
 f_i*f_j=R_{\log(ij)}(b*b),\qquad (b*b)(0)=1 .
\]
Take \(i=2\) and first \(j=2\), then \(j=3\). The two supports lie within \(2\eta\) of \(\log4\) and \(\log6\), respectively. In each support the indicated integer is the only one whose logarithm occurs. Denote the finite-prime term of (16.1) by \(P\). It follows that
\[
 P(f_2*f_2)=-\frac{\log2}{2},\qquad P(f_2*f_3)=0 .
\]
The second convolution still has value one at its centre. Its prime contribution vanishes because \(6\) is not a prime power. Both composed tests enter the polar and real-place terms of \(W\). An operator realisation must compose the actions of the two tests before taking their trace.

theorems.title: Conjecture (Riemann hypothesis)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Conjecture (Riemann hypothesis).** Every zero \(\rho\) of \(\xi\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Re}\rho=1/2\). Equivalently, every centered frequency \(w_\rho\) in (16.2) is real.

theorems.title: Conditional corollary (Weil positivity)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Conditional corollary (Weil positivity).** Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, \(Q(g)\ge0\) for every \(g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)\). Indeed \(\widehat{g*g^*}(z)=\widehat g(z)\overline{\widehat g(\bar z)}\), so (16.2) then sums the nonnegative numbers \(m_\rho|\widehat g(w_\rho)|^2\).

theorems.title: Example (A convolution that detects a double jet)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Fix any complex frequency \(w\) and let \(N\) act on \(\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\) by multiplication by \(\varepsilon\). The Fourier value and its derivative give a two-dimensional action of compact smooth tests,
\[
 \pi(f)=\widehat f(w)I+\widehat f'(w)N .
\]
Indeed \(\widehat{f*g}=\widehat f\,\widehat g\), and the product rule together with \(N^2=0\) gives \(\pi(f*g)=\pi(f)\pi(g)\). On the same two-dimensional space put \(\sigma(f)=\widehat f(w)I\). Both representations have trace twice the product of the Fourier values at \(w\) on every convolution word.

To distinguish the actions, take \(b\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\) with \(\int b=1\) and put \(h(u)=e^{-iwu}b(u)\). Then \(\widehat h(w)=1\). For \(f=ih'-wh\), integration by parts with the positive Fourier sign gives \(\widehat f(z)=(z-w)\widehat h(z)\). Thus \(\sigma(f)=0\), while \(\pi(f)\) sends \(1\) to \(\varepsilon\). Reading the coefficient of \(\varepsilon\) on this input gives one. Closing the same action to a trace gives zero. This calculation applies at any frequency. If a zero of \(\xi\) has multiplicity two, its term in (16.2) supplies the common trace of these two local actions.

theorems.title: Theorem (continuous integer-summation duality)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (continuous integer-summation duality).** The map \(Z\) is a closed topological embedding. Its quotient \(M=E/Z(S_{00})\) is complete and nuclear. Norm-one adelic averaging identifies the actual averaged pole-free lattice-summation image with \(Z(S_{00})\). In \(\mathcal M E\) this image corresponds exactly to the ideal cut out by the preceding vanishing conditions. At each weighted Sobolev stage \(E_n\), the annihilator of the image is the norm closure in \(E_n'\) of the span of these derivative evaluations. The inductive limit of these closed spaces gives the strong continuous dual of \(M\). Evaluation yields a nondegenerate hypocontinuous pairing, continuous uniformly when either argument ranges over a bounded set. It extends to the completed projective bornological tensor product for the bounded sets of these locally convex spaces. [An integer-summation middle complex and its continuous dual][integer-complex]

theorems.title: Theorem (geometric theta trace)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (geometric theta trace).** For every \(f\in\mathcal A_a\), the induced quotient operator \(\Pi_{s,a}(f)\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Tr}_{K_s}\Pi_{s,a}(f)
=\operatorname{Str}_{\mathscr C_s}\Lambda_f=W(f),
\qquad
\|\Pi_{s,a}(f)\|_1\le C_{a,s,\phi}p_{a,4}(f).
\tag{16.8}
\]
Here \(\phi\) is the fixed smoothing cutoff, and the supertrace is the degree-zero trace minus the degree-minus-one trace. [A common Hilbert theta complex, geometric full trace][theta-complex]

theorems.title: The annulus spectrum of translation on the geometric Hilbert quotient
theorems.statement_excerpt:
One can decide whether an equivalent Hilbert norm on this quotient would turn the convolution action into a star representation. Let \(U_t^{(s)}\) be translation by \(t\) on \(K_s\). At every \(1/2<s<\min(a,1)\) and every real \(t\ne0\) its spectrum and its Fredholm essential spectrum both equal
\[
 \{\lambda\in\mathbb C:e^{-s|t|}\le|\lambda|\le e^{s|t|}\}.
\]
In the Fourier representation on the strip \(|\operatorname{Im}z|<s\), translation is the compression of multiplication by \(e^{itz}\) to the Hardy quotient by the inner factor of the theta divisor. Applying the multiplier bound to \(t\) and \(-t\) gives the two radii. For the reverse inclusion, there are unit horizontal intervals containing arbitrarily many zeros counted with multiplicity. Translating those intervals moves their zeros into a fixed box strictly inside the strip, since \(|\operatorname{Im}w_\rho|<1/2<s\). The translated inner factors tend to zero on compact sets, and the translated quotient projections tend strongly to the identity. Projecting a point-evaluation vector and translating it back gives unit vectors tending weakly to zero, on which the adjoint acts arbitrarily close to the conjugate of the corresponding multiplier value, up to a unit phase. These values fill the open annulus, and essential spectrum is closed.

The outer radius exceeds one. Spectrum is preserved by an equivalent norm, whereas a unitary has spectrum on the unit circle. If the integrated tests gave a star representation in that norm, translating a real even approximate identity would make \(U_t^{(s)}\) unitary. Thus changing the norm within its equivalence class cannot produce the desired positive realization. The integrated smooth operators in (16.8) still have their full trace. The strip-width assumption is needed to put the entire translated zero box strictly inside the Hardy strip.

theorems.title: Corollary (cyclic traces on the position–normal algebra)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Corollary (cyclic traces on the position–normal algebra).** Let \(L\) be a \(p\)-torsionfree \(\mathbb Z_p\)-module. Every \(\mathbb Z_p\)-linear trace \(\tau:\mathscr D_h\to L\) satisfying \(\tau(AB)=\tau(BA)\) for all \(A,B\in\mathscr D_h\) vanishes identically.

theorems.title: Theorem (finite-order traces on formal arithmetic disks)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (finite-order traces on formal arithmetic disks).** Fix a prime \(p\) and a finite height \(h\ge1\). On the disk \(c\in\mathbb F_p^h\) in (16.13) put \(d_i=p\partial_{z_i}\) and \(d^\beta=\prod_{i<h}d_i^{\beta_i}\). An operator in \(\mathscr D_h\) has a unique expression on this disk as a finite sum \(\sum_\beta f_{c,\beta}(z)d^\beta\), with \(f_{c,\beta}\in R[[z_0,\ldots,z_{h-1}]]\). Every such choice on the finitely many disks gives an operator in \(\mathscr D_h\). Write \(a_{c,\alpha,\beta}\) for the coefficient of \(z^\alpha\) in \(f_{c,\beta}\). For \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^h\) set
\[
 s(\alpha,\beta)=1+\min_{0\le i<h}
             \{v_p(\alpha_i+1),\,v_p(\beta_i+1)\},
 \qquad v_p(p)=1 .
\]
Reducing each \(a_{c,\alpha,\beta}\) modulo \(p^{s(\alpha,\beta)}\) induces an isomorphism of \(R\)-modules
\[
 HH_0(\mathscr D_h/R)\simeq
 \prod_{c\in\mathbb F_p^h}
 \bigoplus_{\beta\in\mathbb N^h}
 \prod_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^h}R/p^{s(\alpha,\beta)}R .
\]
The direct sum permits finitely many derivative indices \(\beta\) for each operator. At each such index the product permits an arbitrary sequence of Taylor coefficients.

theorems.title: Theorem (fixed whole-window positivity)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Theorem (fixed whole-window positivity).** Every complex \(L^2\) test with essential support in an interval of width at most \(31/10\) satisfies
\[
Q(g)\ge7.0942\cdot10^{-109}\|g\|_2^2.
\]
For the infimum \(\lambda(T)=\inf_{g\ne0}Q_T(g)/\|g\|_2^2\),
\[
7.0942\cdot10^{-109}\le\lambda(31/20)
\le1.705263\cdot10^{-108}.
\tag{16.17}
\]
No assumption on zero locations or simplicity enters. [Local Weil positivity through half-width \(31/20\)][fixed-window]

theorems.title: Proposition (Schur complement)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (Schur complement).** Under the operator-domain hypothesis \(X\subset\operatorname{Dom}W_T\), suppose \(D\ge dI\) for some \(d>0\). Then \(D^{-1}\) is bounded on \(Y\) and has range \(\operatorname{Dom}D\). For each \(u\in X\), completing the square as in (16.18) gives the minimum of \(Q_T(u+v)\) over \(v\in\mathcal Q_T\cap Y\) at \(v=-D^{-1}Ku\). Hence positivity is equivalent to
\[
A-K^*D^{-1}K\ge0.
\tag{16.19}
\]
The correction has quadratic form \(\langle Ku,D^{-1}Ku\rangle\ge0\). In the two-dimensional example (16.18) it was \(c^2x^2\). Positivity of \(A\) bounds the minimum from above. To bound it from below one needs the size of the coupling as well as the positive lower bound on the tail.

theorems.title: A fixed translate test for Weil positivity
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Definition (translated Weil test).** Put \(a_j=2^{-20-j}\), \(j\ge1\), and let \(b\) be the density of the infinite convolution of the uniform probability measures on \([-a_j,a_j]\). Normalize \(\phi(x)=e^xb(x)/\|e^{(\cdot)}b\|_2\). For \(n\ge2\) use the two translates \(g_n=\phi+R_{\log n}\phi\) and denote their Weil reading by \(E_n=Q(g_n)\).

The profile is real and supported in \([-2^{-20},2^{-20}]\) since \(\sum_j a_j=2^{-20}\). Its untilted transform is \(P(z)=\prod_j\operatorname{sinc}(a_jz)\), where \(\operatorname{sinc} v=\sin(v)/v\) and \(\operatorname{sinc}0=1\). The first \(k\) factors give decay of order \(k\) on the real axis, proving smoothness for every \(k\). Since \(\sum_j a_j^2<\infty\), the product converges locally uniformly and vanishes only at the real zeros of its factors. The positive Fourier sign gives \(\widehat\phi(z)=P(z-i)/\|e^{(\cdot)}b\|_2\), which is nonzero throughout \(|\operatorname{Im}z|\le1/2\).

**Theorem (a fixed translate test for Weil positivity).** With \(\log^+ x=\max(0,\log x)\) for \(x>0\) and \(\log^+0=0\),
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \frac{\log^+\max(0,-E_n)}{\log n}
       =\sup_\rho|\operatorname{Re}\rho-\tfrac12| .
\]
To prove the formula, write \(F(t)=W(\phi^**R_t\phi)\). The autocorrelation of the real profile is even, and \(W\) is invariant under reflection. Thus \(F\) is real and even, and the two off-diagonal terms in \(E_n=2F(0)+2F(\log n)\) are equal. In the zero expansion (16.2), the coefficient of \(e^{(\rho-1/2)t}\) in \(F(t)\) is \(m_\rho\overline{\widehat\phi(\bar w_\rho)}\widehat\phi(w_\rho)\ne0\). Its Laplace transform therefore has an actual pole at each \(\rho-\tfrac12\).

Smoothness gives \(|F'(t)|\le Ce^{t/2}\) for \(t\ge0\). Between \(\log n\) and \(\log(n+1)\) the interval has length at most \(1/n\), while the derivative is \(O(\sqrt{n+1})\). A lower bound at the samples thus extends to the intervening times with error \(O(n^{-1/2})\). If the sampled negative parts have exponent below \(\eta>0\), then \(F(t)+C_\eta e^{\eta t}\) is nonnegative on \(t\ge0\) for sufficiently large \(C_\eta\).

The Laplace transform of this nonnegative function has no real pole to the right of \(\eta\), since \(\zeta\) has no real zero in \(0<s<1\). A finite abscissa of convergence of a Laplace transform of a nonnegative function is singular on the real axis. The transform therefore converges throughout \(\operatorname{Re}s>\eta\). An off-line zero giving a pole there would contradict this convergence. Reflection yields one inequality in the formula, and absolute convergence of the zero expansion yields the other.

If all zeros have real part \(1/2\), (16.2) gives \(E_n\ge0\) for every \(n\). Conversely, eventual nonnegativity makes the exponent on the left zero and forces every zero onto that line. The width of \(\phi\) is \(2^{-19}\). It satisfies \(2^{-19}\le1/(2n)\) exactly through \(n=2^{18}\), where the two-interval bound gives \(E_n\ge1/2\) since each copy has norm one. At larger \(n\) further prime powers can enter the cross term. Eventual nonnegativity for this fixed shape remains open.

theorems.title: The fixed Weil test on perfect powers
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let \(E_n=Q(\phi+R_{\log n}\phi)\) for the [fixed translated Weil test](#ch16-fixed-shape-translates), and put \(x_-=\max(0,-x)\). For each fixed positive integer \(q\),
\[
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}
 \frac{\log^+\big((E_{j^q})_-\big)}{\log(j^q)}
 =\sup_\rho\big|\operatorname{Re}\rho-\tfrac12\big|.
\]
The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if \(E_{j^q}\ge0\) for all sufficiently large \(j\).

theorems.title: A four-frequency test on a geometric progression
theorems.statement_excerpt:
At the integers \(4^j\) the gaps on the logarithmic scale stay equal to \(\log4\). Keep \(\phi\) and form a model reading \(E^*_n\) by using just the four frequencies \(\pm\gamma\pm i\beta\), each once, in (16.2). Take \(\gamma=2\pi/\log4\) and \(\beta=1/3\). For \(a=\widehat\phi(\gamma-i\beta)\overline{\widehat\phi(\gamma+i\beta)}\), the real part is the integral of
\[
 \phi(u)\phi(v)e^{\beta(u-v)}\cos\big(\gamma(u-v)\big)
\]
over \(u,v\). Since \(\phi\) is nonnegative and its support has diameter \(2^{-19}\), the cosine is positive throughout that support and \(\operatorname{Re}a>0\). At \(n=4^j\) the phase \(e^{i\gamma\log n}\) equals \(1\), and multiplication of \(n\) by two changes its sign. Adding the four terms and both diagonal readings gives
\[
 \frac{E^*_n}{8\operatorname{Re}a}=
 \begin{cases}
   1+\cosh(\beta\log n),& n=4^j,\\
   1-\cosh(\beta\log n),& n=2\cdot4^j .
 \end{cases}
\]
For example, the ratio is \(25/8\) at \(n=64\) and \(-1/4\) at \(n=8\). All the geometric samples are positive, although the intervening negative readings grow in magnitude like \(n^{1/3}\). The sufficiency of these geometric samples for the zeta spectrum remains open here.

theorems.title: The Weil form on an unbounded sequence of windows
theorems.statement_excerpt: Let \(T_j\) be any sequence of half-widths tending to infinity. If \(\log^+\varepsilon(T_j)=o(T_j)\), every nontrivial zero of \(\zeta\) has real part \(1/2\).

theorems.title: Example (two actions on the same line)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Over a field \(k\), let \(A=k\times k\) and write \(e_1=(1,0)\), \(e_2=(0,1)\). For each \(i=1,2\) give the line \(P_i=k\) its usual right scalar action and let \(A\) act on the left by its \(i\)-th coordinate. Tensoring a complex \(M\) of right \(A\)-modules with \(P_i\) takes its \(i\)-th summand. Explicitly,
\[
 F_i(M)=M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}P_i \simeq M e_i .
\]
The isomorphism sends \(m\otimes c\) to \(c\,m e_i\). The ordinary tensor computes the derived tensor here because \(P_i\simeq A e_i\) is projective. Both functors send the free right module \(A\) to \(k\). Apply them now to its endomorphism \(a\mapsto e_1a\). On \(P_1\) this acts as the identity, on \(P_2\) as zero. Its image \(e_1A\) consequently goes to \(k\) under \(F_1\) and to zero under \(F_2\). The two functors have inequivalent values on this boundary condition. Forgetting the left action identifies their kernels as right \(k\)-modules.

theorems.title: Proposition (operation kernels)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Suppose \(\mu,\nu:\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal S_0\) are enriched \(k\)-multilinear operations preserving colimits in each input. The kernel \(P_\mu=R_0\mu(G_1,\ldots,G_r)\) carries a left \(E_{\rm in}\)-action by applying \(\mu\) to input endomorphisms, as well as its right \(E_0\)-action. For a tuple \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_r)\), form the right \(E_{\rm in}\)-module \(M=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r R_iX_i\), taking tensors over \(k\). Then
\[
 R_0\mu(X)\simeq M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{E_{\rm in}}P_\mu .
\] {#operation-kernels}
Restriction to the full enriched subcategories on the generators identifies the space of homotopy-coherent enriched natural transformations with the derived mapping space of bimodules,
\[
 \operatorname{Map}_k(\mu,\nu)
 \simeq \operatorname{Map}_{E_{\rm in}\text{-}E_0}(P_\mu,P_\nu).
\]
This equivalence includes homotopies between maps and all higher homotopies.

theorems.title: A transformation detected by the residue field
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let \(A=\mathbb Q[x]\). Which input detects a map from the identity functor on derived right \(A\)-modules to its shift? Form the bimodule \(E=Ae\oplus Af\), free on the left, with right action
\[
 e p=p e,\qquad f p=p f+p'e\qquad (p\in A).
\]
The Leibniz rule gives \((fp)q=f(pq)\). The submodule \(Ae\) and the quotient generated by the image of \(f\) are both the diagonal bimodule \(A\). The connecting map of this extension, tensored with each input, gives a natural transformation \(\mathrm{Id}\to\mathrm{Id}[1]\).

On the free right module \(A\), the quotient has the right-linear section \(p\mapsto fp\), so the component of the transformation is zero. A bimodule section would send \(1\) to \(f+he\) for some \(h\in A\). Its failure to commute with \(x\) is the element
\[
 (f+he)x-x(f+he)=e .
\]
Now take the right module \(k=A/(x)\). The sequence splits on the left, so tensoring it with \(k\) computes the derived extension term by term. In the middle term \(\bar f x=\bar e\) and \(\bar e x=0\). Every lift \(\bar f+c\bar e\) of \(1\) has nonzero product with \(x\), so the sequence \(0\to k\to A/(x^2)\to k\to0\) has no right-linear section. The same transformation has a nonzero component on \(k\).

theorems.title: Example (a functor that fails to preserve sums)
theorems.statement_excerpt: On complexes of vector spaces the double dual \(V\mapsto V^{**}\), with \(V^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)\), agrees with the identity on the generator \(k\) and its scalar endomorphisms. Take \(V=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}k\) in degree zero. Then \(V^*=k^{\mathbb N}\), and evaluation sends each vector in \(V\) to a finite linear combination of coordinate functions on \(k^{\mathbb N}\). The constant sequence of ones has nonzero class in \(k^{\mathbb N}/k^{(\mathbb N)}\). Extend that class to a basis and take its coordinate functional. Pulled back to \(k^{\mathbb N}\), the functional vanishes on every coordinate vector but takes the value one on the constant sequence. Thus it lies outside the image of \(V\to V^{**}\). This map is precisely the comparison from the direct sum of the double duals to the double dual of the sum.

theorems.title: Lemma (unit and counit)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Lemma (unit and counit).** \(F\) is fully faithful exactly when \(\eta_L\) is an equivalence for every \(L\). Under that hypothesis the essential image, the objects equivalent to some \(F(L)\), consists precisely of those \(M\) for which \(\varepsilon_M\) is an equivalence.

theorems.title: Example (matrix units)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Example (matrix units).** For the column \(P=k^n\), put \(A=M_n(k)\), \(B=k\), and \(e=E_{11}\), where \(E_{ij}\) sends the \(j\)-th basis vector \(v_j\) to \(v_i\) and kills the others. An \(A\)-linear map \(h:P\to M\) is determined by \(m=h(v_1)\), since \(v_i=E_{i1}v_1\). The equality \(ev_1=v_1\) puts \(m\) in \(eM\). Conversely any \(m\in eM\) defines such a map by \(h(v_i)=E_{i1}m\). Since the column \(P\simeq Ae\) is a summand of the free left module \(A\), this calculation computes \(G(M)\) on complexes as well. Evaluating \(h\) gives the counit
\[
\varepsilon_M:k^n\otimes eM\longrightarrow M,
\qquad v_i\otimes m\longmapsto E_{i1}m.
\tag{17.3}
\]
Its inverse is
\[
M\longrightarrow k^n\otimes eM,
\qquad m\longmapsto\sum_i v_i\otimes E_{1i}m.
\]
The two composites are identities because \(E_{1j}E_{i1}=\delta_{ij}e\) and \(\sum_iE_{i1}E_{1i}=1_A\). The unit sends a vector \(v\) to \(v_1\otimes v\) in \(e(k^n\otimes V)\), so it is also an isomorphism. This proves the equivalence of module categories directly, including its maps.

theorems.title: Conditional theorem (affine induction)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Conditional theorem (affine induction).** Assume a coherent smooth right-\(B\) realization \(\mathcal W\) of \(W\), the prescribed homogeneous endomorphism comparison, compatible Taylor cutoffs for finite diagrams on its Chevalley resolution, and the enhanced tensor–Hom adjunction. Then the unit for \(F=\mathcal W\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\) is invertible on every ordinary unbounded source complex and gives
\[
D(B)\simeq\operatorname{Loc}(W).
\tag{17.4}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\) is generated by \(W\) inside the smooth affine target under shifts, cones, coproducts and retracts, including all internal energy shifts in the graded convention. For a smooth complex \(M\), let \(C_M\) be the cone of the counit \(\varepsilon_M:FGM\to M\) in the smooth affine category. The triangle identity gives \(G(\varepsilon_M)\eta_{GM}=1_{GM}\). The unit is invertible by the theorem, so \(G(\varepsilon_M)\) is an equivalence and \(G(C_M)\simeq0\). By adjunction the mapping complex from any \(F(L)\) to \(C_M\) vanishes. Applying maps from \(F(L)\) to the counit triangle therefore identifies maps into \(FGM\) with maps into \(M\). Since the objects \(F(L)\) exhaust the generated sector up to equivalence, the counit has this factorization property for the entire sector. This is the coreflection in (17.4). [The realization hypotheses](06-duality-and-induction.md#ch06-affine-currents-and-the-algebra-acting-on-their-resolution) · [The original counit](06-duality-and-induction.md#ch06-the-image-and-its-original-counit)

theorems.title: Example (the two vertices)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (the two vertices).** Take arrows \(X_1\xrightarrow{a}X_2\) of \(k[x]\)-complexes. The arrows \(k\xrightarrow{0}k\) and \(k\xrightarrow{1}k\) at \(x=0\) have identical vertex modules. To distinguish them, use the probes \(G_1=(k\xrightarrow{1}k)\) and \(G_2=(0\to k)\), with \(k=k[x]/(x)\). Resolving \(k\) by multiplication by \(x\) identifies the two mapping complexes from the probes with \(\operatorname{fib}(x:X_i\to X_i)\). Precomposition by the map \(G_2\to G_1\) which is the identity at the second vertex induces \(a\) on those fibres. It distinguishes zero from the identity even here.

theorems.title: Theorem (fields on algebraic states)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (fields on algebraic states).** At each \(K\), including \(0\) and \(-2\), the ordered field \(\mathbb Y_-\), translation, vacuum and exchange give a differential graded quantum vertex superalgebra on \(M_3\). A single locality exponent for the first two states works for every final state. The opposite order gives a weakly associative chain field \(\mathbb Y_+\) homotopic to \(\mathbb Y_-\). A full quantum vertex structure for the opposite exchange would require its own identities. [The all-input field theorem](#atlas-c-native-r3-all-input-qva)

theorems.title: The noncritical cohomology field with its trace sector
theorems.statement_excerpt:
To determine the products themselves, compute the states at a fixed \(K\ne-2\). Here \(I_m\) is the \(m\)-th trace-current creation state and \(\xi^I_j\) the \(j\)-th divided translation of the degree-one trace ghost. Let \(\omega_\hbar\) denote the cycle lifting the trace-free cubic ghost. An algebraic chain frame preserves the minimal inclusion and identifies
\[
H^\bullet(M_3)\cong
(R_3\mathbf1\oplus R_3[\omega_\hbar])
\otimes_{\mathbb C}
\left(\mathbb C[I_1,I_2,\ldots]
\otimes\Lambda(\xi^I_0,\xi^I_1,\ldots)\right),
\qquad |\omega_\hbar|=3.
\]
Write \(b=[\omega_\hbar]\) and let \(L\) denote the displayed trace factor. Let \(q_\hbar\) be the degree-two generator of the trace-free small complex. On its translates the differential is \(d(f(T)q_\hbar)=2Tf(T)\omega_\hbar\). Thus \(T\omega_\hbar=d(q_\hbar/2)\), which gives \(Tb=0\). Injectivity of multiplication by \(T\) on \(R_3[T]\) says something further. No nonzero \(f(T)q_\hbar\) supplies another cycle. The product of \(b\) with itself has degree six and stays in the trace-free factor, where the degree-six cohomology vanishes. The chain field factors with the commutative differential field of \(L\). Consequently all cohomology products at fixed \(K\ne-2\) have the form \(Y(x,u)y=(e^{uT}x)y\), with \(b^2=0\). This includes numerical level zero.

theorems.title: Critical states at precision three
theorems.statement_excerpt:
At the critical level \(K=-2\), let \(S\) be the quadratic Sugawara state of the trace-free current algebra. Its jets \(s_j=T^jS/j!\) and degree-one partners \(b_j\), obtained by differentiating the classical differential with respect to level, have weight \(j+2\). Together with the constant degree-three ghost class \(\omega\) they give a different state calculation. As a graded \(R_3\)-module, the full algebraic critical state cohomology is free on the classical monomials of
\[
\mathbb C[s_j:j\geq0]\otimes\Lambda(b_j:j\geq0)
\otimes\Lambda(\omega)\otimes L .
\]
The invariant \(S\) lifts as an actual cycle. Dividing its differential by \(K+2\) before specializing gives a lift of the partner, and applying the binary field to the lifted cycles gives a cycle above each classical basis monomial. One can choose a translation-linear change of state coordinates intertwining the differentials through precision three. This determines the state module and its precision reductions. Determining the singular products and independently produced marked operations at this level remains a further comparison.

theorems.title: A normalized homotopy on the marked retained source
theorems.statement_excerpt:
The short comparison tested inserted ghost degrees zero and one. Let the inserted state \(x\) now have any ghost degree, keeping the whole algebraic current state \(w\in V=M_3^0\) in the rooted slot. Denote the two bulk retained kernels by \(\mathcal Y_-\) and \(\mathcal Y^\sharp\) and their exchange homotopy by \(h^\Lambda\), so that \(\delta h^\Lambda=\mathcal Y^\sharp-\mathcal Y_-\). At a fixed noncritical level \(K\ne-2\) the maps \(i,p,k\) contract the state complex onto the small complex and act as the identity on its trace factor. On that complex the prescribed pure-root kernel \(\Phi\) agrees with \(\mathcal Y_-\). This agreement holds as an operator on every such \(w\). On the cubic generator \(\omega_\hbar\) it follows from invariance of its leading term. On \(q_\hbar\) the current mode of index one differentiates the shifted exchange kernel and supplies the order-two term. Multiplication by a trace-current polynomial and insertion of a trace-ghost monomial preserve both equalities. With \(\Delta=\Phi-\mathcal Y^\sharp\), put
\[
K_{\rm rt}=\Delta k-h^\Lambda ip .
\]
The first term has differential \(\Delta(1-ip)\). The second has differential \((\mathcal Y_--\mathcal Y^\sharp)ip=\Delta ip\). Adding the two terms gives \(\delta K_{\rm rt}=\Delta(1-ip)+\Delta ip=\Delta\). Thus the comparison holds in every inserted degree as a kernel on arbitrary algebraic rooted currents. Its scalar part vanishes because \(\Delta_0=0\) and the degree-one small states have only a trace ghost, paired with a nonnegative trace current which annihilates the rooted input. The homotopy satisfies both translation identities.

A marked coefficient can itself be a Laurent series. At each fixed right quotient and algebraic inserted input require one lower Laurent bound, one ghost cutoff and a common finite set of right current monomials for the whole series. For a series starting at exponent \(\nu\), let \(T_0\) bound the exponents of the retained kernel from below on this finite list of right translates of the rooted state. At output exponent \(t\) the convolution uses only \(\nu\leq j\leq t-T_0\). Homogeneity bounds the ghost indices in each of those coefficients. This supplies the continuity estimate which would fail if new right-current orders or unbounded cutoffs could enter at every coefficient.

On the trace-only inserted summand extend the rooted homotopy by contraction with the dual trace monomials. Each fixed algebraic input meets only finitely many.

On the positive traceless inserted summand the two evaluations use the same prescribed state operation \(\mathcal J\) and Casimir correction \(\Xi\). This gives a homotopy on the indicated whole-series stages of the restricted marked source. The Cartan coordinate isomorphism carries it to the resolved source. On the original unsimplified source one may precompose with the specified current projection. The algebraic homotopy uses the equality of these prescriptions on that summand. A physical junction must compute \(\mathcal J+\Xi\) in each spatial order from its own inputs. This includes the relative maps for a unit in the rooted input, the inserted input and the output, with their prescribed homotopies, as well as the tensorator. [Marked whole-series comparison](#atlas-c-r3-marked)

theorems.title: Proposition (obstruction for the inflated endpoint)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (obstruction for the inflated endpoint).** At every fixed \(K\ne-2\) through \(R_3\), let \(E_3,\overline E_3\) be the two ordered marked evaluations. For \(A^e=A\otimes_{R_3}A^{\rm op}\), write \(\beta_A:\mathcal C\to\mathcal K[1]\) for the connecting morphism of the corner sequence. Then
\[
\beta_AE_3[1]=\beta_A\overline E_3[1]\ne0
\quad\text{in}\quad
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A^e)}
\bigl(\mathcal N_3[1],\mathcal K[1]\bigr).
\]

theorems.title: Two presentations of the marked Gaussian half-space
theorems.statement_excerpt:
In the marked Gaussian half-space both the change of fields and a disk preparation can be computed. Fix numerical \(\hbar,\kappa\ne0\), \(k=\hbar\kappa\), the marking \(\zeta=+i\) and an interior collar profile of integral one. Use oriented transverse coordinate \(t\) and tangential complex coordinate \(z\). In the mixed presentation the tests for the two fields \(\Phi,\eta\) are partial forms in \(dt,d\bar z\). In abelian Chern–Simons theory they are full spatial forms. Every spatial form splits uniquely into a partial form and \(dz\) times a partial form. If \(s\) denotes suspension of the linear tests, the comparison is
\[
s(\alpha e_\Phi)\longmapsto-\kappa^{-1}dz\wedge\alpha,\qquad
s(\beta e_\eta)\longmapsto(-1)^{\deg\beta+1}\beta .
\]
The mixed boundary condition kills the tangential trace of \(\beta\), precisely the condition that the spatial form restrict to a multiple of \(dz\). The change of variables identifies the unary differentials. On a mixed Wick contraction the factor \(k\kappa^{-1}=\hbar\) gives the correct quantum coefficient with the signs from the displayed map. Thus the two complexes of regular compact kernels agree at every fixed field number, with disjoint products and the empty unit. On a proper oriented graph ray the one-form tested by the Wilson source is \(\eta-\kappa^{-1}\Phi\,dz\). The second term contributes when the ray moves tangentially. The ray comparison transports the specified Cauchy propagator, framing and outgoing subtraction with these tests. [The marked Gaussian change of variables](#atlas-c-hz-cs)
