theorems.title: Example (cutting a two-label surface)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let a field on a compact oriented surface be a locally constant label \(1\) or \(2\). Fix dimensionless weights \(w_1=1\), \(w_2=s>0\). A connected component of Euler characteristic \(\chi\) carrying label \(i\) contributes \(w_i^\chi\). Multiply over components and sum over fields with the specified boundary labels. Under gluing one sums over matching labels on each cut circle. These label pairs are precisely the fields on the glued surface, and the Euler characteristics add because a circle has Euler characteristic zero.

Write \(v_i\) for the complex circle state with label \(i\). A pair of pants is connected and has Euler characteristic \(-1\), so \(v_i v_j=\delta_{ij}w_i^{-1}v_i\). In the basis \(e_i=w_i v_i\) this gives \(e_i e_j=\delta_{ij}e_i\). Thus for every \(s\) the circle algebra is \(A=\mathbb C e_1\oplus\mathbb C e_2\), with unit \(e_1+e_2\). Consider its right modules. Taking maps from the projective probe \(e_1A\) returns \(M e_1\) for any complex \(M\). Tensoring back with \(e_1A\) recovers precisely that summand of \(M\). For \(M=e_2A\) this counit is \(0\to e_2A\). Admitting the second probe gives \(M e_1\oplus M e_2=M\), with both projections and all module maps, for every \(s\).

A disk has Euler characteristic one. Its incoming amplitude in the label basis is \(w_i\), so its functional in the idempotent basis is \(\varepsilon_s(e_i)=w_i^2\). Direct summation over the fields on a sphere gives \(1+s^2\). Cutting the sphere into two disks gives the same number by summing \(w_i w_i\) over their common label.

An uncut cylinder has Euler characteristic zero. It carries each label to itself with amplitude one. Present the same cylinder by gluing the pairing \(\beta_s(a,b)=\varepsilon_s(ab)\) on two incoming circles to the inverse pairing on two outgoing circles, along one circle of each. In the idempotent basis the inverse pairing is \(C_s=e_1\otimes e_1+s^{-2}e_2\otimes e_2\). Use instead the inverse pairing \(C_t\) of a theory with weight \(t>0\), identifying the two idempotent bases. The resulting cylinder sends \(e_1\) to \(e_1\), whereas
\[
   \bigl(\beta_s(e_2,-)\otimes 1\bigr) C_t
       =\frac{s^2}{t^2}\,e_2 .
\]
The first probe would accept this cut for every \(t\). The second enforces \(t=s\). The disk sum fixes the value of \(s\) in each theory. [J. Kock, *Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories*, short version, §§1.1.8 and 2.1.4](https://mat.uab.es/~kock/TQFT/FS.pdf#page=8)

theorems.title: Example (four rays at total collision)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Bring four charge-one rays together at level two, with their coordinate frames fixed. On the transverse slice \(X=\mathbb C^3\) the outgoing charge-four coefficient at distinct positions is a rank-one local system. A full turn of a block of \(m\) rays has exponent \(\binom m2/2\) in units of \(2\pi i\). Thus a pair or triple has multiplier \(-1\), whereas all four together have multiplier \(+1\). On a proper normal circle the coefficient differential is monodromy minus the identity, up to orientation. Multiplication by \(-2\) is invertible. For two disjoint pairs there are two independent rotations on the same fibre. Either circle differential contracts the cochains, even though rotating both pairs together acts by \(+1\). In this way the link cochains with the stated coefficient are acyclic at every proper collision. On the punctured slice extension by zero therefore agrees with derived direct image. Call this clean extension \(L\), put \(j:X\setminus\{0\}\hookrightarrow X\), and let \(i\) include the origin. The link \(K=i^*Rj_*L\) records fields on a punctured neighbourhood of the total collision. Here \(V=H^2K\) has dimension two.

What can an observer determine by counting states at the collision? For every line \(W\subset V\), take the perverse quotient \(P_W=j_!L[3]/i_*W\). The shift is the complex dimension of the slice. Its stalk is \(W[1]\), and its costalk in degrees zero and one is \(V/W\) and \(H^3K\), respectively. The dimensions agree for every \(W\). The attaching map tells the extensions apart. For example, fix a basis of the two-dimensional \(V\) and choose each basis line in turn. A dimension counts one state in either stalk. Following that state out to the punctured neighbourhood tests which of the two lines it occupies. In degree \(-1\) the stalk maps into \(H^{-1}(K[3])=V\). The next arrow in the stalk–link–costalk sequence is the quotient \(V\to V/W\), so exactness identifies the image of the attaching map with \(W\). An automorphism of the separated rank-one coefficient acts by a scalar and fixes each line in \(V\). Thus two different lines give distinguishable extensions even with identical state counts.

Exchanging identical rays imposes a different condition. Fix the positive half-exchange as \(+i\). Permutation equivariance leaves the trivial and sign lines. Ordinary pullback from the coarse unordered space requires the stabilizer at the collision to act trivially on the stalk and selects the quotient by the trivial line. Within this family there is a unique answer under that additional hypothesis. [The four-ray calculation](04-factorization.md#ch04-gaussian-collision)

theorems.title: Problem 18.1
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.1.** Construct the adjunction \(F_{\mathrm{phys}}\dashv G_{\mathrm{phys}}\) of the prescribed physical interface. After identifying its source and target, compare it with \(\Phi=\mathcal W\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-:D(B)\rightleftarrows D(\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)):\Psi=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sm}(A_\ell)}(\mathcal W,-)\). Give a natural equivalence \(F_{\mathrm{phys}}\to\Phi\) and its right mate \(\Psi\to G_{\mathrm{phys}}\) on the original complexes. Determine the essential image and compare the tensorators for each of the two spatial orders.

theorems.title: Problem 18.2
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.2.** For an associative chiral algebra \(A\) on ordered configurations, construct its same-position product \(\diamond\) and a coproduct \(A\to A\diamond A\), or a level-indexed family of such morphisms. Require the coproduct to preserve the chiral \(E_1\)-multiplication, exchange, vacuum and iterated collisions. For the completed curved dual, specify the category of contramodules and the classes of morphisms inverted on both sides for which the bar adjunction becomes an equivalence.

theorems.title: Problem 18.3
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.3.** For a pointed factorizing coalgebra \((F,u)\), prove or disprove that \(\Theta:\mathcal X(F,u)\to\mathcal A_C(F,u)\) and \(\Psi:\mathcal A_C(F,u)\to\mathcal X(F,u)\) are inverse equivalences. The remaining homotopy \(\Theta\Psi\simeq\mathrm{id}\) must be natural under restrictions to collision strata and under refinements of ordered partitions. Compare this geometric action space with a mapping space in the localization of ordinary dg vertex algebras only after identifying the objects, pointings and unit fibre on both sides.

theorems.title: Problem 18.4
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.4.** Compare specialization of the integral fusion complex along a partial diagonal with the independently composed line operators at that collision. For the three-pole order \((12)3\), the known maps on \(T=T_{12}\otimes M_3\) are \(L_R(T)\leftarrow L_D^{\mathrm{fac}}(T)\to N_1(T)\), from a common domain to the radial and pair-first completions. Determine where the comparison is an equivalence, with the rational current evaluation and all incoming and outgoing actions intertwined. For integral specialization these morphisms must be defined before the diagonal equation is inverted.

theorems.title: Example (failure of continuous descent)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (failure of continuous descent).** Take the continuous inclusion \(\mu:\ell^1\hookrightarrow\ell^2\) of absolutely summable sequences into square-summable ones, and the functional \(F(x)=\sum_j x_j\) on \(\ell^1\). Its value is well defined on the image of \(\mu\). But a vector with its first \(m\) entries equal to \(1/m\) has \(\ell^2\)-norm \(1/\sqrt m\) and \(F\)-value one. Thus \(F\) cannot extend continuously to the closure in \(\ell^2\). In a channel decomposition it is the norm of the space *receiving* the first sewing that controls the second.

theorems.title: Problem 18.5
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.5.** Let \(\mu:E\to R\) be the actual Virasoro sewing map on a completed source, and let \(F:E\to W\) be a further sewing with \(W\) complete Hausdorff. Determine when \(F\) descends continuously to \(\overline{\mu(E)}\subset R\) on the unsmoothed spaces at real \(c>1\) and positive principal labels. This requires \(F(\ker\mu)=0\) and continuity of the induced map on \(\mu(E)\) in its subspace topology. Compare the resulting composites, including their vacuum channels, on the common domain of the two channel decompositions.

theorems.title: Problem 18.6
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.6.** On the supported contact complex of Chapter 9, compare the compact output \(A_\epsilon\delta_u\) with the elliptic evaluation \(E_\epsilon\delta_c\) in their common Hom complex. Determine whether the residual cochain \(\gamma_\epsilon g_r\delta_c\) in (18.2) can be filled relative to the given lower homotopies and the cylinder evaluation. This requires the full source differential on the contact forms.

theorems.title: Problem 18.7
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.7.** On the numerical gravitational source domain, construct the cut comparison \(\Pi_\epsilon=(1\otimes I_{Q,\epsilon})J_{R,\epsilon}:\mathscr L_{\mathrm{DS},\epsilon}\to\mathscr L_{\mathrm{st},\epsilon}\) from the affine Drinfeld–Sokolov amplitude line to the stress-field line. Here \(J_{R,\epsilon}\) transports the affine semidensity to the cut variables and \(I_{Q,\epsilon}\) integrates the complementary quartet. Require \(T^{\mathrm{st}}_{\epsilon,\delta}\Pi_\epsilon=\Pi_\delta T^{\mathrm{DS}}_{\epsilon,\delta}\) for the two regulator transports. Does this map carry the numerical state with its unnormalized base amplitude to the independently prepared geometric cap and commute with spatial sewing?

theorems.title: Problem 18.8
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.8.** Construct the closed-to-open action of the bulk observables on the brane complexes and compare it with their derived bimodule operations. For the M2 interval at zero Cherednik parameter this means realizing the flux cap \(\omega\frown-:\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\to A_N\) and the junction multiplication \(A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U_N}A_N\to A_N\) with both \(A_N\)-actions and the prescribed outgoing cut.

theorems.title: Problem 18.9
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.9.** Compare the critical Hall coefficient morphism \(p^*(\mathscr P_\alpha\boxtimes\mathscr P_\beta)\to q^!\mathscr P_{\alpha+\beta}\) on the full extension correspondence with its local field operation before applying \(q_!\). Construct its action on the compact state space \(H_d=H^*(S^{[d]},\mathbb Q)\) and identify the reduced three-boundary product there, with its Poincaré pairing and ordinary unit. The comparison must transport the square roots of the determinant lines and the moment parameters on intermediate flags.

theorems.title: Problem 18.10
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Problem 18.10.** Establish positivity of the complete Weil functional for the Riemann zeta function,
\[
W(g*g^*)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C),
\]
or construct a continuous Hilbert-space \(*\)-representation \(\pi:\mathcal A_a/\mathcal J_a\to\mathfrak S_1(\mathcal H)\) with \(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}\pi(f)=W(f)\) throughout the stated arithmetic test algebra.

theorems.title: Problem 18.11
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Problem 18.11.** At a prime \(p\) and finite jet height \(h\), compare the arithmetic collision complexes for \(j_h:R_h\hookrightarrow B_h\) with the collision maps of a local field algebra. The complexes use the factors \([A\to A[f_i^{-1}]]\) for the specified diagonal equations \(f_i\) at each finite precision, followed by \(p\)-adic completion. Require compatibility with the integral normal operators, residue maps, height-raising Frobenius \(\varphi_h:R_h\to R_{h+1}\) and vacuum. On the complex side, identify the common domain of trace-class operators on which the ordinary trace gives the Weil functional. Specify also the continuous jet pairings that detect nilpotent directions at a multiple zero. A comparison between these two coefficient theories must specify the changes of scalars it uses.

theorems.title: Proposition (deformations of the two-state boundary)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let \(S\) be a commutative local Artin \(k\)-algebra in degree zero, with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\) and residue field \(k\). Fix \(x\), \(W\) and the identification of the boundary modulo \(\mathfrak m\) with \(Q\). The odd matrices on the free \(S[[x]]\)-module of rank one in each parity which lift \(Q\) and square to \(W\,1\), up to even changes of basis equal to the identity modulo \(\mathfrak m\), are in natural bijection with
\[
                 \{\,t\in\mathfrak m\mid W(-t)=0\,\}.
\]
The matrix corresponding to \(t\) is \(Q(t)\).

theorems.title: Proposition (higher products of the stabilized residue field)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (higher products of the stabilized residue field).** The boundary endomorphism algebra has a minimal strictly unital \(A_\infty\) model on \(H=k1\oplus k\psi\). It has \(m_0=0\), and minimality means \(m_1=0\). The unit acts by the usual binary product, and operations of arity greater than two vanish on inputs containing the unit. Use the deformation convention \(d\alpha+\alpha^2\), the coordinate \(t\) of \(Q(t)\), and let \([x^n]W\) denote the coefficient of \(x^n\). For \(n\ge2\) the \(n\)-ary product is
\[
 m_n(\psi^{\otimes n})
       =(-1)^{n+1}[x^n]W\;1 .
\]
**Proof.** Write \(\alpha=Q(t)-Q=\sum_{n\ge1}t^n q_n\), so \(q_1=\psi\), and set \(\lambda_n=[t^n](-W(-t))\). Equating coefficients in the square gives
\[
             d q_n+\sum_{i+j=n,\ i,j\ge1}q_i q_j=\lambda_n\,1 .
\]
Define the comparison from \(H\) to the boundary endomorphisms by sending \(\psi^{\otimes n}\) to \(q_n\), the unit to the identity in arity one, and any higher word containing a unit to zero. The displayed equations are its \(A_\infty\) morphism equations on all nonunit words. Indeed, substituting an inner operation of \(H\) produces a scalar unit, so only the linear component can carry that output to the target. The identities for \(H\) itself follow by strict unitality. On a word of odd letters, the only nonzero nested terms multiply an inner scalar on the left or right by the remaining letter, and their two suspended signs are opposite. The linear comparison takes \(1,\psi\) to the cohomology basis above, proving the quasi-isomorphism. Dyckerhoff's one-variable minimal model gives the Taylor coefficients up to signs. Here the entry \(x+t\) and the square \(d\alpha+\alpha^2\) fix them. At a quadratic critical point the same formula gives the Clifford square \(m_2(\psi,\psi)=-[x^2]W\,1\). [The signed bar differential](#ch05-one-differential-encodes-all-associativity-homotopies) · [Dyckerhoff, §5.6, Theorem 5.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0904.4713#page=31)

theorems.title: Example (ordered mixed insertions)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (ordered mixed insertions).** For \(f=x^3,\ g=y^2\) (type \(D_4\)), the three coefficients contributing to \(st^2\) are \(m_3(b,a,b)=1\) and \(m_3(a,b,b)=m_3(b,b,a)=0\). On an auxiliary two-dimensional space attach \(S=E_{12}\) to \(a\) and \(T=E_{21}\) to \(b\). Give both insertions a common even parameter \(u\). The scalar part of their cubic product is \(u^3TST=u^3E_{21}\), since \(S^3=ST^2=T^2S=0\). Their binary product is \(u^2ab\otimes(ST-TS)=u^2ab\otimes(E_{11}-E_{22})\). The \((2,1)\) entry thus distinguishes the ordered cubic word in this representative even though the quadratic obstruction already prevents a flat coupling.

theorems.title: Proposition (endomorphisms of the identity defect)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Proposition (endomorphisms of the identity defect).** Let \(W\in k[[x_1,\ldots,x_r]]\) have an isolated critical point at the origin with \(W(0)=0\). Consider the two-periodic category of matrix factorizations supported at the origin. Its derived centre has cohomology only in even parity, where the cohomology algebra is \(\operatorname{Jac}(W)\). Indeed, telescope \(W(x)-W(y)=\sum_i(x_i-y_i)v_i\). The endomorphism differential of the resulting Koszul factorization sends the contractions to \(x_i-y_i\) and the exterior generators to \(v_i\). On the diagonal the latter are \(\partial_iW\), so the combined sequence is regular. Scalar endomorphisms give the stated algebra. The identity-kernel theorem identifies its cohomology with Hochschild cohomology, and the stabilized residue field is a compact generator at that support. For an isolated point \(p\) of value \(W(p)\), the same statement uses the completed germ of \(W-W(p)\). An identification of the centre including its \(E_2\) operations requires a comparison of cochains. [Dyckerhoff, Proposition 6.3 and Corollaries 6.4–6.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0904.4713)

theorems.title: Example (two higher products and three sphere insertions)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Fix \(dx\) and a potential \(W=x^4+a x^5+b x^6+O(x^7)\). In the marked boundary coordinate the first three scalar products are \(m_4=-1,\ m_5=a,\ m_6=-b\) on copies of \(\psi\), in units of the identity. Suppose instead that the sphere functional at the origin is given on the marked fields \(1,x,x^2\). The critical equation is \(W'=x^3(4+5ax+6bx^2+O(x^3))\), so expansion of the reciprocal gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_W(x^2)&=\tfrac14,\\
 \tau_W(x)&=-\tfrac{5a}{16},\\
 \tau_W(1)&=\tfrac{25a^2}{64}-\tfrac{3b}{8}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The \(x\) insertion fixes \(a\). The vacuum value then fixes \(b\), including the contribution quadratic in \(a\). For \(a=b=1\) these three values are \(1/4,-5/16,1/64\). In this model both calculations start from the same potential. With a sphere functional and higher boundary products supplied separately, the displayed equations test their compatibility in the specified coordinate and volume. Terms of order seven or higher in \(W\) affect none of these three residues.

theorems.title: Example (two colliding vacua)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (two colliding vacua).** For \(W_t=x^3/3-tx\), the monic critical polynomial is \(P=x^2-t\). In \(k[t,x]/(P)\), the residue of an insertion is the coefficient of \(x\) after reduction. Away from \(t=0\) the two roots, in a splitting field, have sphere weights \(1/(2\sqrt t)\) and \(-1/(2\sqrt t)\). Inserting \(x\) multiplies each weight by its own root, so their sum is \(1\). The remainder calculation gives the same value at \(t=0\) and gives \(\tau_t(x^3)=t\), an insertion that reads the splitting parameter.

theorems.title: Proposition (quantum Hamiltonian reduction)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (quantum Hamiltonian reduction).** In this ordering, with \(P(z)=z\prod_{a<n}(z+\zeta_a)\), the protected algebra has relations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 [z,X]&=\hbar X,&[z,Y]&=-\hbar Y,\\
 XY&=P(z),&YX&=P(z+\hbar),
\end{aligned}
\]
**Proof.** In \(XY\) each species contributes \(x_ip_i\). In \(YX\) each contributes \(p_ix_i=x_ip_i+\hbar\). The commutators with \(z=x_np_n\) follow from the \(n\)th Weyl pair, since \(z\) commutes with every other species. The neutral monomials above span the reduction in the forms \(z^b,\ z^bX^a,\ z^bY^a\), with \(b\ge0,\ a\ge1\). To test their independence, invert all \(x_i\) in the ambient Weyl algebra and put \(z_i=x_ip_i\). Its torus invariants are generated by the \(z_i\) and the Laurent powers of \(t=\prod_i x_i\), with \(t z_i=(z_i-\hbar)t\). Indeed a neutral Laurent monomial has the same exponent of every \(x_i\) once its \(z_i\)'s are moved to the left. The differences \(z_a-z_n\) commute with these generators, so imposing \(z_a-z_n=\zeta_a\) gives a map from the original reduction to the skew Laurent algebra in \(z,t^{\pm1}\). There \(X=t,\ Y=P(z+\hbar)t^{-1}\). Different powers of \(X,Y\) have distinct Laurent degrees. In degree \(-a\) the coefficient of \(Y^a\) is the product of the monic factors \(P(z+j\hbar)\) for \(1\le j\le a\). Multiplication by that product is injective, proving independence of the images of \(z^bY^a\), and hence of these elements in the original reduction. The nonnegative degrees give the same conclusion directly. At zero moment parameter and \(n=3\), the order difference \([Y,X]=P(z+\hbar)-P(z)\) is \(3\hbar z^2+3\hbar^2z+\hbar^3\). [Gaiotto and collaborators, quantized Higgs-branch operator algebras](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.15198)

theorems.title: The positive weight string
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Which finite-dimensional Hilbert space representations of this fibre can realise \(z^*=z\) and \(X^*=Y\)? For \(zv=sv\), the commutators give \(Xv\) weight \(s+1\) and \(Yv\) weight \(s-1\) whenever these vectors are nonzero. The product relations give
\[
 \|Xv\|^2=P(s+1)\|v\|^2,\qquad
 \|Yv\|^2=P(s)\|v\|^2 .
\]
In an irreducible representation, start with a lowest-weight eigenvector and apply \(X\) until it vanishes. The span of the string is invariant under \(Y\), since \(YXv=P(s+1)v\), so it is the whole representation. Its weights run from a root \(a\) of \(P\) to \(b-1\), where \(b\) is another root. Each intermediate value \(P(a+1),\ldots,P(b-1)\) must be positive. Here \(P(1)=4\), \(P(2)=0\), \(P(3)=-6\) and \(P(4)=-8\). Only the weights \(0,1\) qualify, and normalising the two vectors fixes the raising coefficient at \(2\). This proves uniqueness up to unitary equivalence.

The representation still allows several preparations. If the two weight populations are \(p_0,p_1\), the readings of \(XY\) and \(YX\) are \(4p_1\) and \(4p_0\). The pure lowest-weight state gives \(0,4\), while the normalised trace gives \(2,2\).

theorems.title: Theorem (four-current algebra through second order)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Theorem (four-current algebra through second order).** Under the fourth-trace hypothesis and coupling relation above, the displayed brackets satisfy Jacobi for every triple of generators and their translates over \(R\). Their vertex algebra has a free \(R\)-basis of ordered monomials in the translated generators.

theorems.title: Proposition (invariant scalar brackets of polynomial Hamiltonians)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
With these covariance and normalization conditions, the brackets satisfying Jacobi are exactly
\[
 [f,g]_t=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{\kappa(t)^j}{(2j+1)!}B_{2j+1}(f,g),
 \qquad \kappa(t)\in t\,k[[t]] .
\]
The first correction \(tB_3/12\) fixes \(\kappa'(0)=1/2\). If the coefficient of \(t^j\) lowers total input degree by \(4j+2\), this fixes \(\kappa(t)=t/2\). Every family with the same first correction takes this homogeneous form in the unique parameter \(t'=2\kappa(t)=t+O(t^2)\).

theorems.title: Corollary (the diagonal class modulo constants)
theorems.statement_excerpt: The first correction \(B_3/12\) gives a nonzero class in the adjoint Chevalley–Eilenberg cohomology \(H^2(\mathfrak h,\mathfrak h)\). A \(k[[t]]\)-linear change of Hamiltonians equal to the identity modulo \(t\) cannot carry the marked bracket to the undeformed Poisson bracket.

theorems.title: Open problem (comparison with the celestial fields)
theorems.statement_excerpt: Can the scalar bracket be realized by operations on the full celestial fields? Its first correction reads a diagonal coefficient of two Hamiltonian variations of the flat one-loop simplex. The ordered mixed pole retains separate output jets, helicities and colours. A comparison would have to reproduce these field operations and their longitudinal descendants. Covariance of the full fields under changes of transverse coordinates, descent to a curved transverse surface and a coproduct for two independently prepared lines each require a compatible field map. An ordered product must retain the unit, so return from Hamiltonians modulo constants to polynomial functions themselves. Even there the normalized Lie bracket leaves the symmetric part of multiplication and the scale of the commutator to be determined. [Ordered angular coefficients](#ch14-celestial-reconstruction) · [The closed-current simple pole](#ch19-closed-current) · [Tensor products of line modules](#ch14-celestial-ordered-transport)

theorems.title: Proposition (associative realization of the scalar bracket)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Let \(A=k[V]\) for a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic \(V\) over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), and let \(0\ne\kappa\in tR\). Consider an associative \(R\)-bilinear product on \(A[[t]]\). Require that it have unit \(1\) and reduce to ordinary multiplication modulo \(t\). Translations and all linear symplectic transformations must preserve it. At each order of \(t\) its coefficient on polynomial inputs must be a bidifferential operator of finite order with polynomial coefficients. Within this class, the products whose commutator is \(dL_\kappa\) for some nonzero \(d\in R\) are precisely the following. Choose \(w\in tR\) with \(w^2=\kappa\) and put \(B_0(f,g)=fg\). Then
\[
 f\star_w g=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{w^n}{n!}B_n(f,g),\qquad d=2w .
\]
Changing \(w\) to \(-w\) reverses the order of multiplication.

theorems.title: Counterexample (shifted-index formula for the axion current)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Counterexample (shifted-index formula for the axion current).** The inner \(E,J\) bracket produces a negative current. Its bracket with the other positive current carries the two simplex weights \(-1/3,-2/3\). The putative higher \(E,J\) term in Fernández–Paquette (B.12) uses the first transverse argument \((3,0)-(1,1)=(2,-1)\), so that prescription gives zero. It leaves the Jacobiator
\[
 \frac{2s\nu}{3}
 \bigl(:L_h[0,0]L_e[1,0]:-:L_e[0,0]L_h[1,0]:\bigr).
\]
The first coefficient is \(-s^3/4\), and the two colour assignments give independent classical ordered monomials. Thus this prescription fails at precisely the first order discarded in the four-current theorem. The unequal jets locate a missing closed-current simple pole. [Fernández and Paquette, (B.12)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.17168v2#page=52)

theorems.title: Theorem (the marked cubic four-current algebra)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
The gauge currents \(J,L\) and the axion currents \(E,F\) are all even. In the pure \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) gauge theory coupled to its axion, fix their brackets through order \(s^2\). Here \(s\) is the axion coupling, \(K(a,b)=\operatorname{tr}_2(ab)\), and \(\nu=-3s^2/8\). Add the cubic \(EJ\) and \(FJ\) brackets and the \(JJ\) correction given above. The resulting brackets satisfy Jacobi through order \(s^3\) for every triple of generators and all their longitudinal derivatives.

Keep the lower brackets and the cubic \(EJ,FJ\) brackets fixed. Consider cubic \(JJ\) corrections with local polynomial coefficients in the field and degree classes allowed by these couplings. A local change of \(J\) starting at order \(s^3\) relates any two solutions of Jacobi in this class. Exactly one correction in this class is equivariant for the prescribed linear transverse \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) action.

Use \(J,L,F\) at all transverse Taylor labels and \(E\) at positive transverse degree. This omits \(E[0,0]\) and all its longitudinal derivatives. Ordered normal monomials in the resulting strong generators and their longitudinal derivatives form a basis of the universal enveloping vertex algebra over \(\mathbb C[s]/(s^4)\). Its vertex products define a translation-equivariant relative chiral algebra on the affine line.

theorems.title: Theorem (quartic poles at transverse degree one)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
Keep the marking above and take the degree-three and degree-two inputs \(p,q\) in that order. Project the quartic \(JJ\) bracket onto two negative fields of total transverse degree one. The result is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mu Q_\xi(B)+d_+Q_\xi(C_+)\\
 &\qquad+d_0Q_\xi(C_0),
\end{aligned}
\]
in units of \(\nu^2\), with
\[
\begin{aligned}
 B&=(16/3,\,4,\,0),\\
 C_+&=(8/3,\,6,\,-2),\\
 C_0&=(8/3,\,-10/3,\,10/3).
\end{aligned}
\]
Reversing the two incoming fields uses the identity \([A_\mu B]=-[B_{-\mu-T}A]\). The double pole has the same tensor with the arguments exchanged. Since \(T\) differentiates both output fields, this reversal contributes one copy of the double-pole tensor to each derivative coefficient. The two simple-pole tensors in the reversed order are therefore \(B-C_+\) and \(B-C_0\), with the arguments exchanged. The projected Jacobi identities hold for all polynomial inputs and all their longitudinal descendants.

theorems.title: Example (three labelled fields)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (three labelled fields).** Put \(u=z_1-z_3,\ v=z_2-z_3\). The cut equations are \(F_1=u(u-v)\) and \(F_2=uv\). They generate \((u^2,uv)\) with radical \((u)\), so \(U_3=D(u)\). The supported complex reduces to \(M\longrightarrow M[u^{-1}]\) in degrees zero and one for a module \(M\) in degree zero. Let \(S=\mathbb C[z_3,u,v]\). For the volume module \(S\,\mathrm{vol}\), the only cohomology is \((S[u^{-1}]/S)\,\mathrm{vol}\) in degree one, containing the simple pole \(\mathrm{vol}/u\). A module supported on \(u=0\) instead has zero localization and survives in degree zero. The Koszul cochain complex of the two equations on \(S\) would give \(S/(u^2,uv)\) in degree two. The locus of failed cuts and the coefficient placed on it both enter the calculation.

theorems.title: Proposition (seventh Betti number of the separating opens)
theorems.statement_excerpt:
**Proposition (seventh Betti number of the separating opens).** For \(n\ge2\) put \(B_i=\binom{n-2}{i}\), taken as zero for \(i>n-2\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_7(U_n)&=2B_4+28B_5+57B_6\\
          &\quad+28B_7+6B_8 .
\end{aligned}
\]
The weight-eight part has dimension \(B_6\) and the weight-twelve part dimension \(4B_5+5B_6\). The remaining classes have weight ten.

theorems.title: Example (obstruction to lifting a marked map)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Example (obstruction to lifting a marked map).** Even if two products \(\mu_{B,s},\mu_{A,s}\) are separately associative, a map \(f_s:B_s\to A_s\) must satisfy \(f_s\mu_{B,s}=\mu_{A,s}(f_s\otimes f_s)\). Fix the flat endpoints \(B_s=k[[s]][u]/(u^2)\), \(A_s=k[[s]][v]/(v^2-s^2)\), with \(u\) identified with \(v\) at \(s=0\). They agree modulo \(s^2\). To lift the marked identity, write \(f_s(u)=v+s(a+bv)+s^2w\) modulo \(s^3\). At order \(s\) its square has coefficient \(2av\), so \(a=0\). At order \(s^2\), \(v^2=s^2\) supplies the unit, whereas \(vw+wv\) in the special fibre belongs to \((v)\). Thus \(f_s(u)^2\) cannot vanish modulo \(s^3\). The two algebras exist to all orders and the marked map lifts through first order only.

theorems.title: Lemma (derived-complete comparison)
theorems.statement_excerpt: **Lemma (derived-complete comparison).** Let \(C\) be the cone of a marked comparison over \(R=k[[s]]\). Assume that \(C\) is derived \(s\)-complete. At each order \(N\), require that the cone of the compatible comparison at that order is the derived reduction \(C_N=C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/(s^N)\). If the comparison on the special fibre is a quasi-isomorphism, the formal comparison is a quasi-isomorphism as well.

nodes.label: Fields at colliding points
nodes.description: A double pole tests the first derivative of a weight when two points meet. A term supported on their diagonal disappears when the points are kept distinct.

nodes.label: Products and higher relations
nodes.description: Bar records multiplication by contracting adjacent factors. Cobar recovers a connected algebra through the finite filtration by word length.

nodes.label: Modules and interface maps
nodes.description: The unit compares a module with the result of induction followed by its right adjoint. The counit compares the reverse round trip with a module on the receiving side. A physical interface must realize the relevant functors.

nodes.label: Actions and vacuum evaluation
nodes.description: Evaluation sends an action to a character. Recognition asks whether multiplication by that character recovers the entire pointed action.

nodes.label: Inputs for repeated operations
nodes.description: An algebraic tensor uses finitely many independent spectator states. A Laurent series formed after tensoring can have a new spectator state in every coefficient.

nodes.label: Fields and coproducts
nodes.description: A coproduct gives an action on two representations. In the spectral example the two levels combine in order and the tensor carries a cross contraction.

nodes.label: Vacua and collision extensions
nodes.description: Ordinary geometric reconstruction uses the family of realized vacua and its maps over every marked configuration.

nodes.label: Composition of junctions
nodes.description: Derived tensor product retains both outer actions. For particle junctions it also detects a degree-two flux class.

nodes.label: Extensions and compact states
nodes.description: A Hall product uses the space of extensions. A compact three-point operation can distinguish products whose prescribed traces agree.

nodes.label: The full Weil trace and its sign
nodes.description: The theta quotient realizes the full Weil functional. Positivity asks whether its value on every convolution square is nonnegative.

nodes.label: States and filling amplitudes

nodes.label: The physical bulk

nodes.label: Which repeated product detects the interaction?

diagrams.title: Independent input momenta and the vacuum diagonal

diagrams.title: The Vandermonde map before and after duality
diagrams.caption: On the affine line with its chosen coordinate, the Vandermonde for one Heisenberg current with zero central contractions in the Cousin differential takes exterior coefficients to symmetric coefficients. Transposing this isomorphism reverses the arrow and the vacuum triangle.
hypotheses: One Heisenberg species over \(\mathbb C[\kappa]\), a finite position set \(I\), and \(n\) polar factors on the affine line with its chosen coordinate. The Cousin differential has zero central contractions. Duals retain their inverse system of finite stages.
relations: On a cut the transposed multiplication contains \(C_{J|K}^\sharp\) on the dual of the entire localized external coefficient.
diagrams.status: Supported pro-duality is proved. The forward comparison with the original regular exterior contact is open.

diagrams.title: Two framed sheets in opposite orders
diagrams.caption: Fix \(T_1=I+E_{12}/u\) and \(T_2=I+E_{21}/u\). Both orders give \(E_{12}+E_{21}\) at \(u^{-1}\). The upper-left entry at \(u^{-2}\) is one in \(T_1T_2\) and zero in \(T_2T_1\).
hypotheses: Inverse parallel transport along increasing \(t\), fixed frames at the two ends, a fixed direction of the oriented line, and the same nonzero spectral displacement \(u\).

diagrams.title: Which cuts separate three ordered points?
diagrams.caption: Let \(x\ne y\). At \((x,x,y)\) the cut \(12|3\) separates its blocks. At \((x,y,x)\) neither consecutive cut does so, since positions 1 and 3 are equal. The common complement is the whole diagonal \(\Delta_{13}\), including points away from the triple collision.

edges.label: Include the open for the cut after 1
Include the open for the cut after 2
Include the diagonal of the first and third points

hypotheses: Smooth curve; external input order 1,2,3; only consecutive cuts.

witness.conclusion: Both consecutive cuts fail, although the point is outside the small diagonal.

diagrams.title: Reconstructing connected coefficients by consecutive cuts
diagrams.caption: With three positive factors there are two gaps. Mark each gap as a separator or leave it inside a word. In the associated graded of cobar of bar the two choices at the first gap are joined by the identity, so the square contracts. The same contraction works for every word of length greater than one. At arity \(n\) the filtration ends at length \(n\). With the empty coefficient fixed to \(k\), bar and cobar recover the objects and their mapping spaces.

diagrams.title: The four triangles for the positive ideal of sl₃
diagrams.caption: For \(B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\) with \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), three positive factors of weights \(1,2,1\) survive and the fourth tensor power vanishes. Start at \(T_4(L)=0\). At each step the scalar-extension unit \(u\) identifies the cofiber as an inflated \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\)-complex. Under (6.1) the affine unit \(\eta\) is invertible on those cofibers. The four triangles give \(\eta_L\) on any unbounded \(L\).

diagrams.title: Multiplication by a character and evaluation on the boundary vacuum
diagrams.caption: Evaluate \(\Theta(g)\) on the boundary vacuum \(u_B\). The right-unit identity returns \(g\), giving \(\Psi\Theta\simeq1\). In the opposite order one must recover the whole action, including its path at the actor pointing \(u\). This holds on the recognized families. The separate roof comparison for one exterior generator acting on rank-one \(V_\kappa\) at \(\kappa\ne0\) has components indexed by charge and constant, each with additive fundamental group \(\mathbb C\) and zero higher homotopy groups.

relations.text: \(\Theta\Psi\simeq1\) on the genuinely unital Chevalley family, its specified module extensions, and the nonunital families of Chapter 7.
Full recognition for every pointed factorizing actor, with all roots and refinements.

diagrams.title: Splitting three ordered levels in two ways
diagrams.caption: Begin at \(V_{\eta_1\eta_2\eta_3}\). Either path sends \(a\) to \(\eta_2\eta_3a_1\otimes\eta_3a_2\otimes a_3\). Each binary tensor uses the scalar cross contraction and the right coaction with tail \(n_{(1)}m_{(1)}\) on \(m\otimes n\).
hypotheses: Flat Hopf algebra with bijective antipode over a characteristic-zero coefficient algebra.
Translation, unitary spectral coquasitriangular form and level automorphisms satisfy all displayed identities in Chapter 12.
The fields and all finite products have the specified common rational germs and expansion domains.

diagrams.title: Two projections of a Hall extension
diagrams.caption: The projection \(p\) (arrow 1) reads the quotient and the chosen subobject. The projection \(q\) (arrow 2) forgets the subobject. Its fibre over the plane \(\mathbb F_3^2\) has four points, one per line. For a complex subobject variety, (15.1) integrates the rational-valued input weights with compactly supported Euler characteristic.
hypotheses: The constructible-function integral uses finite charge support and an actual domain on which Euler integration is defined.
For vanishing-cycle complexes one must also specify the oriented coefficient map (15.2), its support and its degree shift.

diagrams.title: Which zeros contribute to each trace?
diagrams.caption: Each real centered zero of multiplicity \(m\) contributes to \(m\) Hilbert coordinates in the positive representation. The full trace also includes every nonreal centered zero. Equality for all tests is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.

nodes.label: Full Weil trace
nodes.description: \(W(f)=\sum_\rho m_\rho\widehat f(w_\rho)\).

nodes.label: Critical-line trace
nodes.description: \(\operatorname{Tr}\pi_{\mathrm{crit}}(f)=\sum_{w_\rho\in\mathbb R}m_\rho\widehat f(w_\rho)\). At a double critical zero the first two layers each contribute one copy of the Fourier value.

nodes.label: Nonreal remainder
nodes.description: \(\mathcal R(f)=\sum_{w_\rho\notin\mathbb R}m_\rho\widehat f(w_\rho)\). Subtract the critical trace from the full trace on the same test, as in (16.12).
